role.title: Staff Manufacturing Engineer, Primary Structures
role.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team:  

 The Stage Manufacturing team turns design into reality, owning the build of Terran R’s primary structures. This isn’t about turning the same bolt every day; it’s about building the systems to build the rocket. Engineers and technicians work side by side, with deep collaboration and real-time feedback, to shape how we build better and faster. With a manifest and a launch date, it’s up to the team to deliver on Terran R: solving challenges in real time, optimizing for scale, and constantly improving processes. As the vehicle evolves, so will the factory, with opportunities to apply automation, machine learning, and advanced technologies. What we build here sets the blueprint for the future of scaled launch.   

 About the Role: 

 
 Provide Design for Manufacturing feedback to structures teams during the development phase and through the first prototype and flight builds. 

 Collaborate closely with a diverse team of engineers specializing in design, manufacturing, and reliability, as well as internal production teams and external vendors, leveraging their collective expertise to drive progress.  

 Cover the shop floor for all primary structure work center assembly work, clearing barriers and keeping production moving. 

 Champion process improvements across multiple work centers to improve assembly operations and incorporate feedback and learnings from the first Terran R build  

 Create work instructions, specifications, and best practices across multiple high-fidelity processes. Help standardize processes across the manufacturing team 

 
 About You: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, aeronautical, mechanical engineering, or other engineering discipline  

 8+ years progressive and related experience required 

 Strong history of supporting complicated assembly builds and capable of making risk decisions on a regular basis to disposition issues during build and keep production moving 

 Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with engineering and manufacturing groups to understand process constraints and provide design inputs for improved manufacturability  

 Strong engineering fundamentals in statics, mechanics of materials, process improvement/factory design, fastening and joining, machining.   

 Expert knowledge of common drilling and trim ops, other manufacturing processes, tools, inspection methods and GD&T 

 
 Nice to haves but not required:    

 
 Direct experience with forming, welding, drill, trim and fastening operations for aerospace products 

 New product introduction of an aerospace hardware system into a manufacturing, test, and production system with proven success 

 Experience in managing projects in a fast-paced environment 

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here. 

 Hiring Range:
 $143,000 — $215,000 USD 


 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 

 If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at accommodations@relativityspace.com . 

 Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission - via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee - will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.

role.title: Chief of Staff, Production
role.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 About the Role

 The Chief of Staff, Production is an extension of the SVP of Production, a force multiplier who increases executive leverage across a hyper-growth organization. This role exists to create the operating structure, decision clarity, and organizational follow-through that allow the SVP to operate at the altitude the business demands.

Today, the Anduril Production organization is scaling rapidly. Problems are solved quickly because senior leaders engage directly, but that model doesn't scale. The Chief of Staff will drive the transition from an organization that depends on executive participation in every thread to one where leaders own outcomes, escalations are high-quality, and the SVP focuses on the decisions only they can make.

This is a role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, structures chaos without slowing things down, and can absorb executive context fast enough to credibly represent the SVP's intent and standards. You are the glue between the SVP, the Production leadership team, and the rest of Anduril, down and in within the org, up and out across the company.

 What You’ll Do

 
 Context Management: Maintain continuity across every active thread, know what matters, what decisions were made, who owns what, and where escalation is needed. Triage the information overload that floods toward the SVP and proactively surface only what requires their direct engagement.

 Operating Structure: Design and drive the operating cadence for the Production organization: leadership meetings, QBRs, strategic planning cycles, internal business reviews, and cross-functional touchpoints (CDR, MRR, PDR, etc.). Build follow-through, accountability, and decision hygiene, not bureaucracy.

 Executive Filtering: Determine where the SVP must engage, where they should adjudicate, and where their directs should own resolution. Improve the quality of escalations so that when the SVP is pulled in, the issue is framed, options are clear, and a recommendation is ready.

 Executive Extension: Represent the SVP's viewpoint credibly in internal forums, cross-functional meetings, and leadership discussions. This requires deeply internalizing the SVP's standards, priorities, and decision-making patterns, not just relaying messages.

 Communications & Content: Own communications from the Production leadership team, all-hands content, email updates, and departmental rollouts. Create presentations for QBRs, executive meetings, and offsites. Translate complex operational realities into clear narratives.

 Strategic Initiatives: Lead high-impact, cross-functional initiatives from scoping through execution. Drive strategic projects that don't have a natural owner but are critical to the organization's evolution.

 External Engagement & Events: Plan and execute VIP engagements, customer visits, investor visits, department summits, and all-hands events. Own end-to-end logistics, agenda design, and content curation.

 Organizational Development: Help leaders prepare better, escalate smarter, and own outcomes, so the organization matures from reactive to operational.

 
 Qualifcations

 
 5+ years of progressive professional experience in strategic operations, business leadership, management consulting, or directly supporting senior executives in high-growth, complex environments.

 Demonstrated success in a Chief of Staff, or similar executive leverage role, with a track record of transforming how an organization operates, not just coordinating across it.

 Technical or operational experience in aerospace, defense, automotive, advanced technology, or similar hardware-intensive industries.

 Proven ability to absorb executive context rapidly, operate with incomplete information, and accurately represent senior leadership's intent and judgment to the broader organization.

 Exceptional executive communication skills, you distill complex, ambiguous situations into clear, actionable recommendations in writing, presentations, and live conversation.

 Track record of building operating structure around fast-moving leaders, creating scalable systems, decision hygiene, and accountability without slowing the organization down.

 Self-driven and relentlessly proactive. You operate with high autonomy in ambiguous environments, see gaps before they become problems, and drive results without close oversight.

 Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

 
 Preferred Qualifications

 
 Bachelor's degree in a Science, Engineering, or related field; MBA or other advanced degree is a plus.

 Previous success as a Chief of Staff directly supporting C-suite or SVP-level executives in defense or technology companies.

 Familiarity with production environments, manufacturing operations, or hardware development lifecycles.

 Experience in organizations with significant government relations or regulatory components.

 US Salary Range
 $220,000 — $292,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


  

 Data Privacy

This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 The Deployments Team orchestrates the global fielding of Anduril’s cutting-edge hardware and software products. Operating at the critical intersection of product innovation and mission execution, we manage forward logistics, complex site installations, comprehensive maintenance & repairs, field inventory management, and reverse logistics. Working in close partnership across Product, Engineering, Growth, Business Development, Technical Operations, and Mission Operations, the team is central to ensuring unparalleled customer and mission success, directly shaping the future of Anduril’s defense solutions.

We are seeking a Senior Manager of Deployment Operations to join our rapidly expanding team in Ashville, Ohio. In this pivotal leadership role, you will be instrumental in defining and executing the strategic vision for deploying Anduril’s people and technology across a global operational footprint within a specific division. You will build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team, fostering a culture of operational excellence and continuous improvement. This role demands exceptional strategic planning, the ability to navigate complex, often ambiguous challenges, and a relentless focus on scaling operations to meet the demands of our expanding product lines and global missions. You will be a critical bridge between strategic objectives and field execution, ensuring the precise deployment of resources to achieve mission success.

This is a unique opportunity for a transformational leader who thrives in high-growth, high-stakes environments. This is a function maturation and growth role as much as an operating one, and the work rewards depth. The position requires a strong problem-solving mindset, enough technical depth to follow the work of the engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic systems, and the judgment to make decisions whose impact reaches beyond your own team and the current planning cycle. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 Lead and Grow the Function: Lead Product Operations across the Frontier Systems portfolio, managing multiple teams and driving the growth of both sustainment capability and resourcing across the division. Own hiring, performance, development, and organizational design, while also maturing the function itself: the operating model, the standards, and the capability of the people in it.

 Own Service Quality, Internal and External: Hold accountability for the quality of product support delivered to external customers and to internal Anduril teams. Understand the work at every level, both how it is expected to be done and how it is actually being done, and close the distance between the two.

 Scale Support Operations Across the Portfolio: Think strategically about how support scales across the division's full portfolio, current and future. Extend Product Operations coverage to new products and programs as they reach fielded maturity, standing up scope, coverage, escalation paths, and support infrastructure where none exists. All while holding service quality steady as the fielded population grows.

 Align Capacity to Demand: Align support headcount demand to measured support volume, fielded asset population, and product delivery schedules. Own annual headcount planning for the function and produce defensible demand calculations when planning cycles call for them.

 Own the Failure Signal and the fielded product Reliability Loop: Own the workflow that converts field failures into structured, trustworthy signal for product and reliability engineering, spanning failure mode classification, root cause corrective action cycle performance, and recurrence measurement. Partner with engineering to abstract individual incidents into systemic improvements, holding engineering partners accountable to the signal provided and your own organization accountable to its fidelity.

 Set the Support and Sustainment Standard: Establish and enforce the standards by which the organization triages, diagnoses, escalates, and resolves product incidents, including the severity discipline that determines what reaches engineering and when. Mature the sustainment approach for complex electromechanical products supporting the evolution of maintenance, spares and hardware action, configuration and calibration management, and the self-service and tooling investments that reduce support burden over time.

 Sponsor Function Initiatives: Outline and sponsor the initiatives that mature the function, defining the end state, the measure of success, and the resourcing. Then hold program management partners accountable for leading and delivering the targeted outcomes. 

 Be the Interface for Support Requirements: Serve as the point of contact program teams come to when assessing product and customer service support requirements for new and expanding programs. Characterize the cost of the service and define the contract and pricing structures that fund it, in support of proposals and modifications.

 Brief Executive Stakeholders: Represent product support to business line and division leadership through recurring reviews of fleet health, reliability trends, sustainment cost, and the maturation of the service. Surface systemic problems with evidence, drive cross-functional prioritization, and help deeply technical teams, program stakeholders, and operators in the field understand each other.

 Travel and Availability: Ability to travel up to 20% to support customer needs and operations, and to work non-standard hours when fielded operations require it.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 Proven Technical Leadership: 8+ years of professional experience managing, mastering, and supporting complex technical systems (robotics, aerospace, defense, automotive, or other electromechanical domains).

 Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, industrial, or field support).

 Organizational Leadership: Experience leading managers and multi-team organizations, with accountability for outcomes across more than one product line or program.

 Incident Workflow Ownership: Experience owning incident-driven workflows at a standard-setting level, including triage, diagnosis, severity assignment, escalation, and resolution across a fielded fleet.

 Technical Depth: Enough technical depth to follow the work of engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic and electromechanical systems, including the ability to reason across hardware, software, and networking boundaries.

 Reliability Workflow Familiarity: Demonstrated familiarity with product improvement or reliability lifecycles and processes.

 Sustainment Approach: Experience defining a sustainment model for fielded hardware across its service life, spanning maintenance, spares, and the tooling or self-service investments that reduce support burden.

 Capacity and Cost Modeling: Experience building and defending quantitative models that size support demand, headcount, or cost, including owning annual planning for a function and stating the assumptions behind the model.

 Program Management: Project and program management ability applied outside a project management role: decomposing requirements into deliverables, synthesizing information from several sources into a clear recommendation, and driving that recommendation to a result across multiple functions.

 Executive Influence: Proven ability to align senior cross-functional leadership and influence outcomes without authority over the people who deliver them, including briefing executive stakeholders on operational performance.

 Communication: Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills, and confidence navigating ambiguity and establishing new ways of working where none exist.

 Clearance: Active or eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret Security clearance. Holding clearances or background investigations in the past is a plus.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:

 
 Experience establishing a product support or sustainment function from the ground up, including defining the operating model, growing the team, and running remote support operations for complex robotics systems.

 Defense, law enforcement, or other government agency experience leading air defense, intelligence, and/or force protection teams.

 Consulting or process maturation project experience, and formal training or certification in a continuous improvement or project management disciplines (such as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Agile, or PMP).

 Fluency with structured root cause methods such as fault tree analysis, fishbone, or 8D problem solving.

 Working knowledge of reliability engineering fundamentals, including failure distributions, mean time between failure and maintenance, and reliability growth.

 Hands-on exposure to the failure behavior of fielded robotic and sensor systems, including actuation, power systems, sensing, embedded compute, radar, RF detection, and electro-optical and infrared sensing, and the ability to diagnose connectivity and networking faults across distributed field systems.

 Comfort reading logs, telemetry, and test data, including hands-on use of Linux command-line interfaces and tooling such as Grafana, Datadog, Jira, Git, SQL, and Palantir Foundry.

 Experience translating support scope into contract or pricing structures for operations and sustainment, and familiarity with proposal efforts.

 Fluency with the data layer of sustainment, including incident management systems, asset and configuration data, service bill of materials, and cost association.

 Experience in on-call support operations and limited risk tolerance environments.

 An active U.S. Secret clearance or higher, prior military service, or a defense and STEM background.

This role is the architect of that system.

 THE ROLE 

 The Senior Manager, Warehouse Ops Excellence is the management system architect for the MMF organization. You will also serve as the operational chief of staff to the Director, Material Movement & Flow — translating strategic priorities into structured execution through the operating rhythm, decision-support packages, and organizational readiness tracking. You will design and stand up the operating rhythm, continuous improvement methodology, training infrastructure, and KPI framework that warehouse operations runs on. Once each system is established, you will coach and empower the line to maintain and evolve it independently — your success is measured by how well the systems run without you in the room.

 You will also shape the broader MMF organization as it scales — defining functional charters, role boundaries, and operating frameworks that new teams and leaders will inherit, including future inventory integrity and control leadership roles. You will architect the operating model across multiple buildings and programs as construction completes, partnering with Material Flow Engineering to ensure new spaces launch with the management system already in place.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO 

 
 Operating Rhythm: Design and facilitate the tiered daily management system — DOR, WOR, and MOR. Own templates, cadence, escalation paths, visual boards, and action tracking.

 Tier System & Leader Standard Work: Build the tier board system, leader standard work schedules, and escalation protocols. Coach supervisors and team leads on structured daily accountability.

 Toyota Kata & Continuous Improvement: Serve as the team’s Kata coach. Own the CI pipeline — Kaizen events, A3s, and savings validation.

 Production Program Accountability : Build the governance framework that defines how production programs engage with warehouse operations — SLAs for material availability, handling requirements, turnaround commitments, and regulatory compliance. Develop the scorecarding methodology and hold program leads accountable to it. Serve as the warehouse-to-planning interface alongside the MFE team.

 Training System Architecture: Design the qualification system: skills matrices, standard work documentation, onboarding programs, and train-the-trainer certification. Partner with the Warehouse Manager to build training capability within the existing team — identify and develop supervisors and team leads as certified trainers, and define the dedicated training roles the organization will need as it scales.

 KPI Design & Analytics: Define and visualize metrics across all warehouse functions using the SQDIP framework. Own the calculation methodology. Provide labor and budget analysis including headcount modeling and cost-per-unit metrics.

 Management System Audits: Design and execute layered process audits. Track standard work and leader standard work compliance. Identify systemic gaps and drive corrective actions.

 Change Management: Lead rollout of new processes, SOPs, and WMS/ERP system changes. Own communication plans, training requirements, and post-implementation verification.

 Multi-Building Operating Structure: Architect the operating model across multiple buildings and programs as the site builds out. Ensure consistency in management systems, WMS/ERP configuration, and process standards across all facilities. Partner with MFE on layout, storage strategy, and systems integration.

 Organization Design: Partner with the Director to define functional charters, role boundaries, reporting structures, and operating models for new teams and leadership positions as the organization scales.

 Director's Chief of Staff: Serve as the Director's operational chief of staff — maintain the org readiness tracker, prepare briefing packages for WOR and MOR, coordinate cross-functional priorities, and surface risks through the operating rhythm rather than ad hoc escalation. Ensure the Director's time is focused on strategic decisions by driving the structured cadence that keeps day-to-day execution on track.

 Budget Process: Own the MMF operating budget build — assemble inputs, prepare quarterly forecasts, and track actuals versus plan.

 Cross Team Collaboration:  Collaborate with cross-functional teams, which requires regular interaction with production and manufacturing stakeholders and frequently working directly on the production floor.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 7+ years in operational excellence, lean manufacturing, production system deployment, or warehouse/manufacturing operations, with 3+ years in a leadership role.

 Expertise in TPS principles: Kata coaching, A3 problem-solving, Kaizen facilitation, and standard work development.

 3+ years designing and facilitating tiered daily management systems (DOR/WOR/MOR or equivalent).

 Experience building training and qualification systems in a manufacturing or warehouse environment.

 Proficiency with KPI design, dashboards, and translating data into operational action.

 Experience with ERP/WMS platforms and managing process changes through system transitions.

 Strong analytical skills: labor modeling, budget analysis, and cost-per-unit tracking.

 Excellent communication and coaching skills across all levels — shop floor to site leadership.

 Demonstrated ability to operate as a chief of staff or right hand to a senior leader — synthesizing information, driving meeting cadence, and ensuring leadership bandwidth is protected.

role.title: Sr. Manager, Mission Engineering & Operations
role.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good. 

 At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

 Your Impact 

 You will lead a team of Mission Engineers who serve as Axon’s embedded builders and operational partners inside strategic public safety agencies. Mission Engineers work face-to-face with the people doing the work, diagnose how the agency operates, and build the workflows, automations, integrations, and AI-enabled solutions that measurably improve it.

 As Senior Manager, you will create the environment in which that work succeeds. You will coach experienced individual contributors, set a clear bar for technical delivery and agency partnership, and help the team turn ambiguous field problems into secure, maintainable solutions that reach production and earn sustained adoption. You will stay close enough to the portfolio to recognize patterns, anticipate risk, and connect what the team learns in the field back to Product, Engineering, and the broader organization.

 Success is reflected in agencies becoming more capable, Mission Engineers growing into trusted transformation leaders, and strong field solutions becoming reusable patterns that benefit customers beyond a single engagement. Axon’s mission is to Protect Life, and this team is one of the most direct ways we advance that mission alongside the agencies we serve.

 What You’ll Do 

 Location: Southeast US Regionally based with Travel up to 40%
 Reports to: Senior Director, Customer Deployment & Mission Engineering
 Direct Reports:   Individual Contributors

 Lead, Coach, and Develop Mission Engineers

 
 Lead and develop a distributed team of embedded Mission Engineers working across strategic agency environments

 Coach individual contributors through complex technical decisions, ambiguous customer problems, executive conversations, and high-stakes delivery moments

 Establish clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, onsite partnership, production delivery, adoption, documentation, and measurable agency impact

 Build individualized development plans and create opportunities for Mission Engineers to expand their technical range, executive presence, and transformation leadership

 Foster a culture of curiosity, candor, responsible experimentation, continuous learning, and shared accountability

 Support thoughtful team growth by selecting and onboarding people who can both build practical solutions and earn credibility with agency stakeholders

 
 Set the Bar for Agency Outcomes

 
 Ensure Mission Engineers begin with the agency’s mission, operational workflow, and desired outcome before selecting or building a solution

 Require clear baselines, success criteria, and adoption measures so impact is demonstrated rather than assumed

 Guide the team from discovery through production use, iteration, handoff, and sustained adoption

 Help Mission Engineers balance immediate agency needs with secure, maintainable, and scalable solution design

 Reinforce that success means the agency is more capable—not that one individual has become indispensable

 
 Own a Strategic Mission Engineering Portfolio

 
 Maintain visibility across strategic agencies, active builds, adoption progress, technical risk, and emerging operational needs

 Match Mission Engineer capability and level to agency complexity, transformation opportunity, and stakeholder environment

 Use operating reviews and portfolio data to identify delivery risks, recurring friction, adoption barriers, and opportunities for reuse

 Step into critical situations with structure and calm while coaching the accountable Mission Engineer to remain in ownership

 Drive consistent execution across embedded engagements without forcing every agency problem into the same playbook

 
 Advance Technical and AI-Enabled Delivery

 
 Maintain sufficient fluency across SaaS, cloud services, APIs, enterprise integrations, hardware, data, and modern AI tooling to coach technical decisions and challenge weak reasoning

 Help the team decide when to configure the platform, when to extend it, and when a net-new build is justified

 Establish expectations for validation, observability, fallback paths, maintainability, documentation, and responsible use of sensitive data

 Ensure solutions uphold CJIS requirements, evidence integrity, privacy, approved-tooling standards, and other applicable security controls

 Encourage practical use of AI to accelerate work while preserving human ownership of architecture, accuracy, and outcomes

 
 Turn Field Learning Into Organizational Leverage

 
 Build mechanisms for Mission Engineers to document and share reusable workflows, integrations, frameworks, and playbooks

 Identify patterns across agencies and help convert successful one-off solutions into repeatable capabilities

 Create strong feedback loops with Product and Engineering around recurring workflow friction, unmet operational needs, and product opportunities

 Partner with Mission Operators, Customer Success, Deployment, Professional Services, Support, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Enablement so agencies experience coordinated execution

 Share portfolio insights with senior leaders to influence investment, prioritization, staffing, and the evolution of the Mission Engineering operating model

 
 Lead Executive and Agency Engagement

 
 Build trusted relationships with command staff, agency executives, technical leaders, and internal senior leadership

 Serve as a senior partner during agency-impacting incidents, high-visibility deployments, and moments that require clear trade-offs or executive alignment

 Translate complex technical and operational issues into decisions that are clear to both technical teams and executive audiences

 Coach Mission Engineers to challenge requests constructively, communicate candidly, and leave stakeholders with a practical path forward

 
 What You Bring

 Required

 
 10+ years of experience in customer-facing technical delivery, systems integration, solutions engineering, implementation consulting, operational transformation, or comparable environments

 5+ years leading and developing senior technical individual contributors in customer-facing organizations

 Demonstrated success coaching teams that deliver secure, production-ready solutions in complex customer environments

 Experience leading distributed or field-based teams across multiple customers, regions, or engagement models

 A record of improving technical execution, adoption, operational outcomes, and delivery consistency across a portfolio

 Broad technical fluency across SaaS platforms, cloud services, APIs, networking, hardware, integrations, data workflows, and AI-enabled technologies

 Executive presence with the ability to earn trust, communicate trade-offs, and guide decisions with command staff and senior leaders

 Strong systems thinking and the ability to distinguish isolated issues from patterns that require a scalable solution

 A data-informed leadership approach using baselines, production delivery, adoption, operational improvement, quality, and reuse to evaluate performance

 Comfort leading through ambiguity while creating clarity around ownership, priorities, and success criteria

 Ability to obtain and maintain CJIS compliance and exercise sound judgment with highly sensitive information

 
 Preferred

 
 Experience in public safety, law enforcement, defense, government technology, or another mission-critical operating environment

 Familiarity with CAD, RMS, digital evidence, real-time operations, or integrated public safety ecosystems

 Experience leading teams that build automations, integrations, operational workflows, internal tools, or AI-enabled solutions

 Experience converting field-developed solutions into reusable frameworks, product improvements, or organizational playbooks

 Familiarity with technical talent development, competency frameworks, or academy-style enablement programs

 
 Additional Information

 We recognize that leaders may arrive through different paths. If you have developed technically curious customer-facing teams, helped people turn ambiguous operational problems into working solutions, and care deeply about measurable customer impact, we encourage you to apply.

 Benefits that Benefit You

 
 Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

 Discretionary paid time off

 Paid parental leave for all

 Medical, Dental, Vision plans

 Fitness Programs

 Emotional & Mental Wellness support

 Learning & Development programs

 And yes, we have snacks in our offices

 
  

 Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.
 Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

 Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Important Notes 

 The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions. 

 Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment. 

 We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at  axongreenhousesupport@axon.com  or via our  Axon Privacy Web Form . For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our  Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice. 

 Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment. 

 We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes. 

 Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers .  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com , or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com .

role.title: Head of Technical Operations (TechOps)
role.description:
Join Formlabs if you want to bring ground-breaking professional 3D printers to the desktop of every designer, engineer, researcher, and artist in the world.

 As the Head of Technical Operations (TechOps) at Formlabs, you will own the foundation the whole company runs on: our global network, on-premise servers, endpoints, IT service desk, identity and access, and the security program that protects Formlabs and our customers’ data. This is a single, combined leadership role — where you will lead as a player-coach.

 You will lead a global team of 7 spanning network administration, systems administration, help desk, and cybersecurity, and support offices in Somerville, Germany, Budapest, and Shenzhen.

 You will join the Systems team, which enables every Formlabs team with enterprise applications, infrastructure, data, AI, and security. You will report to the CIO.

 This role is based in our Somerville, MA office and is an onsite role. 

 The Job: 

 
 Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop a team of 7 across network, systems, help desk, and cybersecurity. Set clear priorities, build strong technical leadership within the team, and grow the team’s automation and scripting skills.

 Network & Connectivity: Own our Cisco Meraki estate across four countries — SD-WAN and site-to-site VPN, firewalls, segmentation, Wi-Fi, ISP circuits, cloud VPN tunnels, remote access, and the specific connectivity and compliance requirements of operating in China.

 Strategy & Roadmap: Define and drive a combined infrastructure and security roadmap that balances reliability, risk, cost, and user experience — and explain it in business terms to the CIO, CFO, and company leadership. 

 Servers & Resilience: Own on-premise compute (Proxmox) and the services that run on it — lifecycle, patching, monitoring, backup and tested restores, and disaster recovery — and make deliberate decisions about what stays on-prem versus moves to cloud or SaaS.

 Security Program: Own Formlabs’ cybersecurity program end to end: policy, risk register, vulnerability and patch management, endpoint protection, email and SaaS security, logging, data loss prevention, and incident detection, response runbooks, and exercises.

 Staffing Model & Services: Provide leadership on how the team is staffed and which services it relies on — deciding what to build in-house versus source from managed service and security partners — and hold those partners accountable to clear scope and SLAs.

 Identity & Access: Own the joiner/mover/leaver process, SSO and MFA, privileged and break-glass access, and admin hygiene across Google Workspace and core SaaS — with the evidence trail auditors expect.

 IT Service Desk & Endpoints: Ensure a fast, friendly, measurable help desk for ~800 employees — ticket SLAs, onboarding/offboarding, laptop lifecycle and MDM, conference room and A/V, and site support — and personally own the hardest escalations.

 Automation & AI: Replace manual, repeatable work with automation and AI-assisted workflows across provisioning, monitoring, ticket triage, and reporting, so the team scales with the company.

 Vendors & Budget: Own the infrastructure and security vendor portfolio and budget — contracts, renewals, licensing, and hardware refresh plans — and make clear build/buy/partner tradeoffs.

 Documentation & Continuity: Maintain current diagrams, inventories, runbooks, and on-call/escalation coverage so no system depends on a single person’s knowledge.

 
 You: 

 
 Experience: 8+ years in IT infrastructure and/or security, including 2+ years leading teams, ideally in a mid-sized (500–2,000 person) company with multiple international sites.

 Network & Systems Depth: Hands-on expertise in enterprise networking (routing, VPN, firewalls, segmentation, Wi-Fi) and server virtualization; you can review a firewall rule set or a backup design yourself.

 Security Leadership: Practical experience building or running a security program at a company without a large dedicated security team — including EDR, identity, vulnerability management, and incident response.

 Service Mindset: You care how employees experience IT, measure service quality, and lead a help desk with the same rigor as a network.

 Vendor Management: Proven ability to design a team’s staffing and sourcing model, and to select, negotiate with, and hold managed service providers accountable.

 Communication: Translate technical risk into clear business decisions for executives, and write clear policies, runbooks, and recommendations.

 Controls & Compliance: Experience with frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, or SOC 2, and with IT general controls in an audit-ready environment.

 Bachelor’s degree in a technical field or equivalent experience.

 
 Bonus Points: 

 
 Experience with Cisco Meraki, Proxmox, CrowdStrike, Google Workspace, and Cloudflare.

 Experience operating IT in China (cross-border connectivity, local regulations, remote-site support).

 Familiarity with GCP and AWS security fundamentals (IAM, logging, network controls).

 Scripting/automation skills (Python, PowerShell, Terraform, or similar) and hands-on use of AI tools in IT or security operations.

 Security certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or CCNP Security.

 Experience in a hardware or manufacturing company with R&D labs and lab networks.

 
 Our Benefits & Perks: 

 
 Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs

 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)

 401K matching and access to financial advisors

 Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)

 Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)

 Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it

 Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

 Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats

 Regular sponsored professional development opportunities

 Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community

 And of course… unlimited 3D prints

 
 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.   

 Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.

 Our Candidate AI Guidelines are available here . Please give them a read.
 Compensation: 
 

 Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.

 Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.

 The annual base pay range for this role is:
 $150,000 — $190,000 USD

role.title: Senior Manager, Regulatory Operations
role.description:
Company Overview: 

 Prime Medicine is a leading biotechnology company dedicated to creating and delivering the next generation of gene editing therapies to patients. The Company is leveraging its proprietary Prime Editing platform, a versatile, precise and efficient gene editing technology, to develop a new class of differentiated, one-time, potentially curative genetic therapies. Designed to make only the right edit at the right position within a gene while minimizing unwanted DNA modifications, Prime Editors have the potential to repair almost all types of genetic mutations and work in many different tissues, organs and cell types.  

 Prime Medicine is currently progressing a diversified portfolio of investigational therapeutic programs organized around our core areas of focus: hematology, immunology & oncology, liver and lung. Across each core area, Prime Medicine is focused initially on a set of high value programs, each targeting a disease with well-understood biology and a clearly defined clinical development and regulatory path, and each expected to provide the foundation for expansion into additional opportunities. For more information, please visit www.primemedicine.com .

 Position Summary

 The Senior Manager, Regulatory Operations will plan, coordinate, and drive execution of regulatory submissions and program timelines across Prime Medicine's product pipeline. This role partners closely with Regulatory Affairs, CMC, Nonclinical, Clinical, and Quality teams to ensure submissions to global health authorities (including the FDA and EMA) are complete, high-quality, and delivered on schedule. The ideal candidate brings strong project management discipline, deep familiarity with regulatory submission processes, and the ability to keep cross-functional teams aligned under tight timelines.

 Key Responsibilities

 
 Submission Planning & Execution: Lead end-to-end planning and execution of regulatory submissions, including INDs/CTAs, BLAs/MAAs, amendments, annual reports, and briefing packages.

 Timeline & Risk Management: Develop and maintain integrated regulatory timelines, track milestones and dependencies, identify critical-path risks, and drive mitigation plans.

 Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner with Regulatory Affairs, CMC, Nonclinical, Clinical, Quality, and external partners to compile, quality-check, and finalize submission content.

 Health Authority Interactions: Support preparation for health authority meetings, including briefing books, logistics, meeting minutes, and action item tracking.

 Information Requests: Track incoming health authority information requests (IRs) and coordinate timely, well-organized responses across functional teams.

 Document & Systems Management: Manage regulatory publishing and document management systems, ensuring submissions meet eCTD and other applicable technical standards.

 Process & Compliance: Maintain regulatory operations SOPs and tracking systems; identify and implement process improvements to increase efficiency and quality.

 Vendor & Budget Oversight: Support management of regulatory operations vendors and budget, including publishing and translation vendors.

 
 Required Qualifications

 
 Bachelor's degree in life sciences, regulatory affairs, or a related field.

 7+ years of experience in regulatory affairs or regulatory operations within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

 Demonstrated experience managing IND/CTA and BLA/MAA submissions from planning through filing.

 Strong working knowledge of eCTD structure, regulatory publishing tools, and document management systems (e.g., Veeva Vault RIM or similar).

 Proven project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent programs and competing priorities.

 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management abilities.

 High attention to detail and a strong quality mindset.

 
 Preferred Qualifications

 
 Experience supporting rare disease or orphan drug development programs.

 Experience with gene therapy, gene editing, or cell therapy regulatory submissions.

 Experience with expedited programs such as Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, RMAT, or Orphan Drug Designation.

 PMP or other formal project management certification.

 Advanced degree (MS, PharmD, or PhD) in a scientific discipline.

 Experience working with global (ex-US) health agencies, such as the EMA, MHRA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, or PMDA.

 The pay range reflects the full-time base salary range we expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. Base pay will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, skills, and education. This role is eligible for an annual short-term incentive award (e.g., bonus) and an annual long-term incentive award (e.g., equity).

 Prime Medicine offers a comprehensive Total Rewards package with robust health, financial, and wellness benefits—including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) match, and equity programs—along with generous paid time off, wellness days, and company-wide recharge breaks.

 Our commitment to employee well-being reflects our belief that when we care for our people, we strengthen our ability to put patients first and make meaningful impact together.

 U.S. Pay Range
 $149,000 — $166,000 USD 


 Prime Medicine is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by law.

role.title: Director, Power Plant Operations - Memphis
role.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

 DIRECTOR, POWER PLANT OPERATIONS 

 The Director, Memphis Power Plant Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the gas turbine power generation facility supporting SpaceXSI's Colossus data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee. This role oversees all plant operations, maintenance, commissioning, and continued construction/expansion of the dedicated power plant, with full ownership of delivering reliable, high-availability electrical power to the Colossus AI training clusters. The position is responsible for driving operational excellence, ensuring 24/7 power reliability and quality, safety, environmental compliance, and leading cross-functional teams to achieve aggressive scale-up, availability, cost, and schedule objectives in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Memphis gas turbine power plant, including 24/7 operations, maintenance, commissioning, and ongoing construction and capacity expansion

 Own end-to-end delivery of electrical power to the Colossus data center sites, ensuring industry-leading reliability, availability, power quality, and redundancy

 Lead multidisciplinary teams of operators, maintenance technicians, engineers, contractors, and support staff in a 24/7 operational and construction environment

 Oversee plant performance, commissioning, testing, and seamless integration with data center electrical infrastructure and load

 Develop and execute comprehensive operations and maintenance strategies, including preventative/predictive maintenance, outage planning, hot gas path management, and OEM coordination for gas turbines, generators, balance of plant, and high-voltage electrical systems

 Manage concurrent construction, equipment installation, civil works, and phased capacity expansions while maintaining safe, reliable operation of the existing plant

 Ensure full compliance with environmental, safety, and regulatory requirements, including air permits, emissions controls, TDEC, EPA, OSHA, and local authorities

 Partner closely with SpaceXSI data center operations, engineering, fuel suppliers, OEMs, utilities, and regulatory agencies

 Formulate and execute operating budgets, fuel management, O&M, capital projects, and annual operating plans

 Drive continuous improvement in plant availability, heat rate, emissions, cost, safety metrics, and operational processes

 Establish and promote a culture of uncompromising safety, accountability, operational excellence, rapid execution, and collaboration

 Serve as the site leader and primary representative to the Memphis community, regulators, and stakeholders

 Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing talent; manage staffing, resource allocation, and contractor oversight for both operations and construction

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, or other engineering discipline

 8+ years of experience in power generation operations, plant management, or industrial or aerospace operations

 5+ years of leadership experience managing teams of operators, technicians, and engineers

 Experience operating or managing gas turbine power plants (simple cycle or combined cycle)

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Experience managing large-scale gas turbine facilities (100 MW+), preferably with high-availability critical power applications (data centers, industrial, or similar)

 Proven track record of achieving and sustaining high plant availability, reliability, and low forced outage rates

 Hands-on experience with plant construction, commissioning, start-up, and concurrent operations/expansion of gas turbine facilities

 Deep knowledge of gas turbine technology (aeroderivative and/or heavy-duty frames), performance optimization, emissions controls (SCR, etc.), and balance of plant systems

 Experience with high-voltage electrical systems, generators, switchgear, protection, and data center or industrial interconnection

 Strong understanding of environmental permitting, air quality compliance, and regulatory reporting for combustion turbines

 Experience in fast-paced, high-growth environments requiring simultaneous operations and major construction

 Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, fuel costs, contractors, and complex stakeholder relationships

 Excellent oral and written communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills

 Unfazed by major, abrupt changes in strategic direction or aggressive timelines

 Ability to work in a demanding, autonomously driven, start-up atmosphere

 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

 
 Ability to support and supervise plant operations and construction outside of normal business hours, including nights, weekends, and on-call response

 Must be based at the Memphis, TN site

 Willingness to work extended hours as needed to support plant reliability and construction milestones

 General physical fitness required; ability to walk the plant site, access equipment, and work in industrial/outdoor environments (heat, noise, etc.)

 SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our  Recruitment Privacy Notice .

role.description:
About Commonwealth Fusion Systems: 
 
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy.
 
Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future.
 
We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world.
 
Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. 
 
If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you.


Join the power movement as Senior Manager, Accounting Operations
 
Our Accounting team is looking for a transformational leader to own and optimize our operational accounting functions. This person must have a broad knowledge of accounting and experience in developing and scaling a talented team. The Senior Manager, Accounting Operations acts as a connector between our Accounting function and adjacent teams including Payroll, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, etc. We are looking for someone who is anticipatory and able to look five steps ahead in the process to see how accounting decisions affect everything part of our organization. The role is structural in nature: it creates one clear owner for work that is currently fragmented across staff, consultants, and senior accounting leadership, reducing operational bottlenecks and helping the Accounting organization scale as CFS grows.You will lead us through optimization efforts to develop and implement best practices and effective systems as we continue to scale the company, but also won't be afraid to be hands-on when necessary. This role has immense opportunity for growth as our team continues to grow and develop.

What you'll do:
Evaluate, recommend, and implement process improvements for accounting operations, including analyzing potential system enhancements and developing SOPs
Own collaboration with Supply Chain, FP&A, People Ops, IT, etc. to ensure optimized processes and cross-functional communication
Manage and develop the AP, payroll, expense reporting, and state filing compliance team and operations; build role clarity, cross-training, backup coverage, and accountability
Serve as the first-line manager-level owner for operational accounting issue triage, escalation handling, root-cause follow-up, and process discipline
Document key operating procedures, create scalable SOPs and training materials, and ensure process changes are communicated and adopted across impacted functions
Monitor operational accounting metrics and recurring issues to identify trends, reduce rework, and improve processing accuracy and cycle time
What we’re looking for:
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or Accounting or similar field preferred
Minimum of 7 years of relevant accounting, accounting operations, or finance operations experience
Minimum of 5 years of supervisory, team lead, or process-owner experience in a finance/accounting environment
Hands-on experience with AP, payroll coordination, expense reporting, state filing compliance, or related operational accounting workflows
Demonstrated experience improving processes, resolving operational bottlenecks, documenting procedures, and driving accountability across functions
Experience working cross-functionally with teams such as Supply Chain, FP&A, People Ops/HR, ERP/IT, operations, or procurement
Strong process ownership, issue triage, prioritization, and root-cause problem-solving skills
Ability to manage ambiguity, create structure, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment
Strong communication skills and ability to partner with non-accounting stakeholders while maintaining compliance and control discipline
People leadership, coaching, staff development, and accountability management
Strong Excel and ERP fluency; ability to use data to identify exceptions, trends, and process gaps
Bonus points for: 
Experience in a high-growth, manufacturing, R&D, project-based, or operationally complex environment
Experience with Odoo or similar ERP systems
Experience managing external providers for state filings, compliance, payroll support, or related services
Experience with corporate card programs, travel and expense systems, procure-to-pay workflows, or payroll systems
CPA, CPP, or other relevant professional certification
Experience building SOPs, training materials, controls documentation, and audit-ready support

Perform extended activities such as typing, standing, sitting, walking, etc.

The Manufacturing Quality Director provides strategic leadership and oversight of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational excellence, product reliability, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement. This position is responsible for developing and executing quality strategies, driving improvements in internal and external quality metrics, and reducing the overall cost of quality.
As a key member of the plant leadership team, the Manufacturing Quality Director partners with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Product Management, Supplier Quality, Technology, Distribution, and Service to establish quality objectives, resolve complex quality issues, and ensure alignment with business priorities.
The Director is accountable for manufacturing quality performance, execution of the quality operating plan, continuous improvement initiatives, and leadership and development of the Quality organization.
This role supports plant operations in LaFayette, GA. 
 Position 
Manufacturing Quality Director 
 Location 
USA, LaFayette, GA 
 
 How You'll Create Possibilities 
 Quality Strategy and Operational Leadership 
 Develop and execute manufacturing quality strategies aligned with plant and business objectives.
 Provide leadership and direction for quality performance across manufacturing operations.
  
 Establish measurable quality objectives, performance targets, and improvement plans to support operational excellence.
 Partner with plant leadership and cross-functional teams to integrate quality requirements into manufacturing processes and business decisions.
 Drive accountability for quality performance through effective communication, performance reviews, and corrective action plans.
 Promote a culture of quality ownership, continuous improvement, and proactive problem-solving throughout the organization.
  
 Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement 
  
 Own and drive improvement of key internal and external quality metrics, including First Pass Yield (FPY), Cost of Quality (COQ), Service Call Rate (SCR), scrap, Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), and product damage.
 Analyze quality performance data to identify trends, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.
 Lead the development and execution of corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans to address quality concerns and prevent recurrence.
 Ensure timely containment, root cause analysis, and permanent corrective actions for End-of-Line Audit (EOLA) findings and other manufacturing quality issues.
 Drive year-over-year improvements in quality performance, process capability, and manufacturing efficiency.
 Champion Lean principles, structured problem-solving, error-proofing (poka-yoke), and proactive quality tools to reduce defects and improve process reliability.
  
 Cost of Quality and Financial Accountability 
 Own the development and execution of the manufacturing Cost of Quality operating plan.
 Identify and prioritize opportunities to reduce scrap, rework, warranty exposure, product damage, and other quality-related costs.
 Establish improvement initiatives targeting the highest contributors to quality losses.
 Partner with Operations, Finance, Engineering, and other stakeholders to evaluate financial impacts and deliver sustainable cost reductions.
 Monitor performance against quality cost targets and implement corrective actions to address unfavorable trends.
 Drive resolution of quality-related concessions attributable to manufacturing operations and implement strategies to prevent recurrence.
  
 Quality Management Systems and Process Control 
 Ensure manufacturing operations comply with established Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, applicable ISO standards, and internal quality procedures.
 Provide oversight of the Manufacturing Change Process (MCP), ensuring changes are appropriately evaluated, documented, approved, communicated, and implemented.
 Partner with the Change Implementation Board (CIB) and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain effective change control and documentation compliance.
 Identify critical manufacturing processes requiring control plans and ensure appropriate controls are established, documented, and maintained.
 Ensure manufacturing quality standards, procedures, and control plans remain current and are consistently followed.
 Support continuous improvement of quality systems, process controls, and manufacturing standards to minimize operational risk.
  
 Cross-Functional Quality and Customer Support 
  
 Collaborate with Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, Product Engineering, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering, Field Quality, Distribution, and Service to resolve quality issues impacting manufacturing operations and customers.
 Partner with Supplier Quality to address supplier-related defects, assess proposed supplier changes, and ensure appropriate change control and production readiness.
 Work with Field Quality and Service organizations to identify emerging product concerns, evaluate field performance, and implement effective manufacturing countermeasures.
 Ensure appropriate quality controls are established for product rework, reprogramming, and corrective actions performed at supplier facilities, distribution centers, or other locations.
 Support resolution of Technical Assistance Group (TAG) concerns and other field service issues attributable to manufacturing processes.
 Collaborate with Engineering to recommend improvements to product testing requirements and manufacturing controls based on field performance and customer usage.
 Leverage technical expertise across the organization to accelerate problem resolution and achieve quality objectives.
  
 People Leadership and Organizational Development 
 Lead, develop, and manage the Manufacturing Quality organization, including Quality Leaders, Quality Engineers, technical specialists, and other supporting personnel.
 Establish clear performance expectations, responsibilities, and development objectives aligned with departmental and business priorities.
 Provide coaching, mentoring, and performance feedback to strengthen technical capabilities, leadership effectiveness, and accountability.
 Ensure appropriate staffing, resource allocation, and prioritization of quality initiatives to meet operational requirements.
 Build a high-performing quality organization focused on collaboration, continuous improvement, and measurable results.
 Promote employee engagement, knowledge sharing, and the development of future quality leaders.
  
 Performance Monitoring and Business Reporting 
 Establish and maintain effective daily, weekly, and monthly quality performance reviews.
 Monitor key performance indicators, identify unfavorable trends, and ensure timely escalation and resolution of significant quality concerns.
 Communicate quality performance, improvement initiatives, risks, and corrective action progress to plant and business leadership.
 Translate complex quality data into actionable business insights and improvement priorities.
 Ensure quality initiatives are executed within established timelines, budgets, and performance expectations.
  
 Leadership Expectations 
  
 Demonstrate ownership and accountability for manufacturing quality performance.
 Influence decisions and drive results across multiple functions and organizational levels.
 Balance immediate operational quality requirements with long-term strategic improvement objectives.
 Exercise sound judgment in evaluating quality risks, business impacts, and resource priorities.
 Foster collaboration, operational discipline, and continuous improvement.
 Develop organizational capability through effective leadership, talent development, and succession planning.
 
 
 What You'll Bring to Our Team 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline; equivalent combination of education and relevant technical experience may be considered.
 Experience in Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Reliability, Product Service, or a related technical function.
 Demonstrated experience with root cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies.
 Ability to analyze technical and quality data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Demonstrated ability to work effectively across multiple functions and organizational levels.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and technical investigations simultaneously.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and PowerPoint.
 Knowledge of PFMEA, Control Plans, CAPA, SPC, and other quality systems and tools.
 Experience supporting New Product Introduction and product reliability initiatives.

role.title: Sr. Manager, Healthcare Quality Assurance
role.description:
We are currently looking for a Full Time Sr. Manager, Healthcare Quality Assurance to join our Healthcare Quality Assurance team located at the Newcastle Medical Center working 8:00AM-5:00PM - Mo Tu We Th Fr.

**Summary:** 
The Sr. Manager, Healthcare Quality Assurance is responsible for evaluating healthcare facilities, clinical operations, equipment, and support services to ensure compliance with federal, state, accreditation, and organizational standards. This position will conduct inspections, audits, investigations, and quality assessments to improve patient safety, regulatory compliance, operational efficiency, and healthcare outcomes. The role works closely with clinical leadership, facilities management, infection prevention, biomedical engineering, environment of care, and regulatory agencies to identify deficiencies and implement corrective actions.

**Responsibilities:** 

* Conducts comprehensive inspections and quality assurance audits of healthcare facilities, departments, and operations
* Evaluates compliance with standards established by organizations such as: The Joint Commission, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid, OSHA, NFPA, and FGI
* Inspects patient care areas, utility systems, medical equipment, life safety systems, infection control practices, and environmental conditions
* Reviews policies, procedures, maintenance records, inspection reports, and regulatory documentation
* Identifies deficiencies, risks, and non-compliance issues and prepares detailed corrective action recommendations
* Leads or assists with mock surveys, accreditation readiness activities, and regulatory inspections
* Monitors performance improvement initiatives and verifies corrective actions are completed effectively
* Prepares detailed written reports, inspection summaries, and compliance documentation
* Provides guidance and training to staff regarding healthcare regulations, safety standards, and quality improvement practices
* Maintains current knowledge of healthcare regulations, accreditation standards, and industry best practices
* Assists leadership in continuous quality improvement and patient safety initiatives
* Performs all other duties as assigned

**Competencies:** 
Essential:
 

* Ability to prepare clear and concise role-specific reports
* Ability to read, understand and interpret architectural, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, civil and structural drawings
* Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills
* Knowledge of mechanical, electrical, plumbing and general building construction trades
* Knowledge of international fire codes (IFC), international building codes (IBC), electrical codes (NEC), and international plumbing codes (IPC)
* Knowledge of infection control procedures
* Knowledge of all applicable regulatory and accrediting agency requirements
* Problem-solving and analytical skills with attention to detail
* Organizational and time-management abilities

**Skills:** 
Essential:
 

* Basic Computer skills
* Must be familiar with the Microsoft Office Suite of products
* Advanced project management skills
* Proficient in compliance tracking software and building automation systems

**Experience:** 
Essential:
 

* 3 years directly related supervisory experience
* 10 years directly related experience

**Education:** 
Essential:
 

* High School, GED or Equivalent

**Credentials:** 
Essential:
 

* CN Core Leadership Level 2
* Pass general background check
* Standard Driver's License
* Building Inspection Certification
* Certified Healthcare Safety Professional

 
 
Essential:
 

* This position requires completion of level two Core Leadership Training within 18 months of the hire or promotion date
* Ability to obtain Building Inspection Certification within 6 months of hire date

**Working Conditions:** 
Essential:
 

* Works in a hospital or clinic environment
* Frequently lift and or carry up to 25 lbs
* Sometimes lift and or carry up to 50 lbs
* Subject to traveling and working at other locations or in other environments
* May be required to work after hours or on weekends as needed
* Pass pre-employment drug test

**Training** 

* It is the responsibility of each employee to attend required training for their position or profession as determined by their line of support (LOS) or the leadership of the Chickasaw Nation. It is the responsibility of those who supervise, manage or otherwise lead employees or teams to ensure each employee has access to and receives all required training.

**Mission, Vision & Core Values** 
**Mission:** 

* To enhance the overall quality of life of the Chickasaw people.

**Vision:** 

* To be a nation of successful and united people with a strong cultural identity.

**Core Values:** 

* The Chickasaw People
* Cultural Identity
* Servant Leadership
* Selflessness
* Can Do Attitude
* Perseverance
* Stewardship
* Trust and Respect
* Loyalty
* Honesty and Integrity
* Teamwork
