role.title: Commissioning Director
role.description:
**About Us**

Clayco is a full-service, turnkey real estate development, master planning, architecture, engineering, and construction firm that safely delivers clients across North America the highest quality solutions on time, on budget, and above and beyond expectations. With $8.1 billion in revenue for 2025, Clayco specializes in the "art and science of building," providing fast track, efficient solutions for mission critical, industrial, life sciences, power & energy, aviation, commercial, institutional, residential and sports & entertainment related building projects.

**The Role We Want You For**

As the Commissioning Director, you will play a pivotal role in overseeing and executing all commissioning activities on-site. Your leadership will ensure that every project is completed efficiently, effectively, and to the highest standards of quality and safety. This role demands extreme ownership and a proactive approach to managing complex commissioning processes.

**The Specifics of the Role**

 

* Develop and Implement Commissioning Plans: Create detailed commissioning plans, estimates, and schedules, ensuring all documentation is accurate and up to date. Engage with the owner early in the project for the development of systems and plant start up. Partner with process engineering in the development of plant turnover systems. Conduct Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) to further define commissioning plans.
* Oversee Daily Activities: Manage daily commissioning tasks on-site, ensuring timely and efficient completion of all activities.
* Coordinate with Teams: Collaborate with the Operations Team and Project Management to address schedule, budget, training, and any emerging issues.
* Inspect and Test Systems: Conduct thorough inspections and tests of equipment and systems to ensure compliance with safety policies and project requirements.
* Manage Deliveries: Coordinate equipment and material deliveries with vendors and subcontractors, ensuring alignment with project schedules.
* Ensure Quality and Timeliness: Perform commissioning activities to meet project delivery schedules, integrating third-party vendors and equipment suppliers effectively.
* Maintain Safety Standards: Uphold the highest safety standards throughout all commissioning processes.
* Provide Leadership: Lead and mentor the commissioning team, ensuring cohesive and effective execution of all tasks.
* Conduct Pre-Commissioning Inspections: Perform pre-commissioning and start-up inspections to confirm project readiness.
* Report Issues: Provide timely updates and reports on commissioning issues to all relevant parties.
* Project Completion Activities: Defines the split of responsibilities between Clayco, CSS, Project Management, and Client.
* Prepare for Client Transition: Prepare turnover packages and support the transition to the client after final inspections and commissioning are complete.
* System Testing: Conduct integrated system testing and compile results to ensure system functionality and performance.
* Additional Duties: Perform other related duties as needed.

**Requirements**

 

* Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Experience: 15-25 years of experience in construction, commissioning, start-up, and operations on large-scale projects.
* Certifications: ANSI CX certification is a plus.
* Specialized Experience: Experience in data center commissioning and Building Automation Systems (Controls) is highly desirable.
* Skills: Proficient in creating, reviewing, and presenting reports related to commissioning activities. Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing commissioning plans for large-scale construction projects.

**Some Things You Should Know**

 

* Our clients and projects are nationwide – Travel will be required.
* No other builder can offer the collaborative design-build approach that Clayco does.
* We work on creative, complex, award-winning, high-profile jobs.
* The pace is fast!
* This position is classified as a safety-sensitive role in accordance with applicable state and federal laws. Candidates selected for this position will be subject to a comprehensive background check, which includes mandatory drug testing.

**Why Clayco?**

 

* 2025 Best Places to Work – St. Louis Business Journal, Los Angeles Business Journal, and Phoenix Business Journal.
* 2025 ENR Midwest – Midwest Contractor (#1).
* 2025 ENR Top 100 Design-Build Firms – Design-Build Contractor (Top 5).
* 2025 ENR Top 100 Green Contractors – Green Contractor (Top 3).
* 2025 ENR Top 25 Data Center Builders - Data Center Contractor (Top 3).

**Benefits**

 

* Discretionary Annual Bonus: Subject to company and individual performance.
* Comprehensive Benefits Package Including: Medical, dental and vision plans, 401k, generous PTO and paid company holidays, employee assistance program, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, disability coverage, learning & development programs and more!

**Compensation**

 

* The salary range for this position considers a wide range of factors in making compensation decisions including but not limited to: Education, qualifications, skills, training, experience, certifications, internal equity, and location. Compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.

Sun Life U.S. is one of the largest providers of employee and government benefits, helping approximately 50 million Americans access the care and coverage they need. Through employers, industry partners and government programs, Sun Life U.S. offers a portfolio of benefits and services, including dental, vision, disability, absence management, life, supplemental health, medical stop-loss insurance, and healthcare navigation. We have more than 6,400 employees and associates in our partner dental practices and operate nationwide.

 

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

 

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

 

Visit our website to discover how Sun Life is making life brighter for our customers, partners and communities.

*DentaQuest manages dental and vision benefits for more than 33 million Americans. Our outcomes-based, cost-effective solutions are designed for Medicaid and CHIP, Medicare Advantage, small and large businesses, and individuals. With a focus on prevention and value, we aim to make quality care accessible to improve the oral health of all.*

**Job Description:**

**Location:** Sun Life embraces a hybrid work model that balances in-office collaboration with the flexibility of virtual work. Our team members and leaders are expected to foster connection and teamwork by being present in the office at least 2 days per week.

 

**The opportunity:**

The Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance leads the Quality Assurance function within Dental Shared Services and is accountable for the consistent execution of quality monitoring, audit, calibration, reporting, and improvement activities across supported operations. This role manages quality teams and programs, translates performance data into actionable recommendations, and partners with Operations, Compliance, Training, Workforce Management, Client Engagement, Technology, and Business Process Outsourcing partners to strengthen controls, address risk, and improve member, provider, client, and business outcomes.

 
 

**How you will contribute:**

* Manage the day-to-day execution and continuous improvement of quality assurance programs across Dental Shared Services and supported operational functions, including Contact Center, Claims, Utilization Management, Provider Operations, Complaints and Grievances, Member Enrollment, Intake and Digital Services, and Vision operations.

* Establish and maintain audit procedures, sampling approaches, quality standards, calibration routines, and reporting practices aligned with contractual, regulatory, client, and internal control requirements.

* Lead, coach, and develop quality leaders and professionals by setting clear expectations, balancing workloads, monitoring productivity and accuracy, and supporting engagement, accountability, and career development.

* Analyze quality results, disputes, appeals, re-audits, and operational trends to identify root causes, emerging risks, and practical opportunities for improvement.

* Partner with Operations, Training, Workforce Management, Compliance, Client Engagement, Technology, and BPO leadership to develop and monitor corrective actions, coaching plans, training updates, and sustainable performance improvements.

* Manage client audit and calibration activities, including call and case selection, audit review, documentation preparation, meeting participation, follow-up, and timely response to client or regulatory inquiries.

* Coordinate quality support for internal, external, regulatory, and client audits; prepare evidence, contribute to management action plans, validate remediation, and track findings through closure.

* Implement quality improvement and technology initiatives, including automation, speech analytics, AWS Contact Lens, end-to-end review models, enhanced reporting, and expanded quality monitoring capabilities.

* Assess staffing, capacity, audit volumes, and competing priorities; recommend resource adjustments that support required coverage, service commitments, and cost-effective delivery.

* Maintain enhanced oversight for high-risk, high-profile, and penalty-impacting clients through targeted audit criteria, clear escalation paths, and proactive communication routines.

* Represent Quality Assurance in cross-functional forums, operational readiness activities, transformation projects, vendor discussions, compliance meetings, and leadership reviews.

* Prepare and present quality results, risks, recommendations, and improvement plans to business leaders, clients, and cross-functional partners.

* Promote a culture of accountability, compliance, continuous improvement, collaboration, and client-focused service delivery.

* Perform other duties as assigned.

 
 

**What you will bring with you:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Operations Management, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

* Seven or more years of progressive experience in quality assurance, healthcare operations, dental operations, contact center operations, claims, compliance, or related business operations.

* Three or more years of leadership or people management experience, preferably in a quality assurance, operations, or shared services environment.

* Experience supporting government, commercial, Medicaid, Medicare Advantage, or other regulated healthcare programs preferred.

* Strong knowledge of quality monitoring, audit methodology, calibration, root cause analysis, corrective action planning, internal controls, and performance improvement practices.

* Experience working with BPO partners, client audits, regulatory audits, and cross-functional operational teams preferred.

* Experience with reporting, dashboards, quality analytics, speech analytics, call recording tools, contact center platforms, or AWS Contact Lens preferred.

* Sound business judgment with the ability to connect quality performance to client, compliance, operational, and financial outcomes.

* Strong people leadership, coaching, performance management, and talent development skills.

* Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, determine root causes, and recommend practical solutions.

* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present findings, risks, and recommendations to leaders, clients, and cross-functional audiences.

* Strong project management, prioritization, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, deadlines, and competing priorities.

* Ability to influence without direct authority and build effective partnerships across Operations, Compliance, Training, Technology, Client Engagement, and vendor teams.

* Demonstrated ability to lead teams through change, implement standardized processes, and support technology-enabled transformation.

* High attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, compliance, confidentiality, and ethical business practices.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, SharePoint, and Teams.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**About Mayzo, Inc.**

Since 1986, Mayzo has been a trusted global supplier of specialty chemical additives and innovative material solutions that help manufacturers create safer, more efficient, and more sustainable products. Our technologies support a wide range of industries by improving product performance, enhancing manufacturing processes, reducing waste, and lowering costs.

As a privately held company, Mayzo combines the agility and entrepreneurial spirit of a growing organization with the stability, reputation, and financial strength built over nearly four decades. Our success is driven by knowledgeable, passionate employees who are committed to solving complex customer challenges through technical expertise, innovation, and exceptional service.

At Mayzo, we believe our people are our greatest advantage. We foster a collaborative, customer-focused culture where employees are empowered to make an impact, develop professionally, and contribute to meaningful work that supports customers around the world. If you're looking to build your career with a company that values innovation, teamwork, and long-term success, we'd love to hear from you.

**About the Role**

**Department**

Operations

**Reports to**

Vice President of Global Operations

**Type**

Full-Time

**Location**

Mayzo Operations Center in Walterboro, SC

**Overview**

Mayzo is seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead the overall performance and continuous improvement of our manufacturing facility in Walterboro, South Carolina. This hands-on leadership role oversees production, safety, quality, maintenance, inventory, shipping and receiving, and employee development. The Plant Manager will ensure products are manufactured safely, efficiently, and in accordance with company standards, customer requirements, and regulatory guidelines while fostering accountability, teamwork, and operational excellence.

This is an opportunity to join a vibrant, privately held company that combines the energy and growth of an entrepreneurial organization with the stability, brand recognition, and solid financial foundation of an established business.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Lead day-to-day manufacturing operations to achieve production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery expectations.
* Monitor production schedules and coordinate labor, equipment, and other resources to optimize workflow and efficiency.
* Build a strong safety culture and maintain compliance with OSHA requirements, environmental regulations, company policies, and safe work practices.
* Lead investigations involving safety incidents, quality concerns, equipment failures, and operational issues, including corrective and preventive actions.
* Ensure compliance with applicable ISO standards, quality management systems, and customer specifications.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, quality, cost reduction, production yield, and operational efficiency.
* Analyze plant performance metrics, including safety, quality, productivity, labor, inventory, equipment utilization, and financial results.
* Develop, coach, and lead supervisors and plant employees through clear expectations, regular feedback, and professional development.
* Oversee preventive maintenance programs and ensure equipment and facilities support safe, reliable, and efficient operations.
* Partner with Supply Chain, Customer Service, Sales, and Procurement to support inventory availability and on-time customer shipments.
* Develop and manage the plant operating budget and identify cost-saving opportunities without compromising safety or quality.
* Support new product introductions, process improvements, capital projects, and other business objectives.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, or another technical discipline required; industrial engineering or logistics is preferred.
* Minimum of 15 years of business and team management experience in the chemicals industry or a related field; small- or mid-sized company experience is preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in supply chain management, operations management, and/or product management.
* Experience with ERP systems, inventory control, warehousing, logistics, and procurement.
* Demonstrated knowledge of manufacturing safety, regulatory compliance, quality systems, budgeting, maintenance, and continuous improvement.
* Proven ability to lead teams, solve complex operational problems, manage projects, and adapt to changing priorities.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Directly supervises employees within the Mayzo Operations Center.
* Recruits, hires, trains, coaches, and evaluates employees; plans and assigns work; recognizes performance; addresses concerns; and takes corrective action when appropriate.
* Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with Mayzo policies and applicable laws.

**Physical Demands and Work Environment**

* Continual standing and walking, with frequent climbing, balancing, bending, stooping, kneeling, or crawling.
* Ability to lift, push, or carry items up to 25 kg (approximately 55 lb.) without assistance.
* Frequent work around fumes, airborne particles, toxic chemicals, production machinery, and loud noise with required PPE.
* Use of specialized equipment or vehicles, including forklifts and scissor lifts.

**Benefits**

* Health, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k)
* Flexible Spending Account and Health Savings Account
* Life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* Paid time off

**Core Competencies**

* People leadership and employee development
* Safety, quality, and regulatory focus
* Operational and financial management
* Problem solving and sound decision-making
* Project management and execution
* Adaptability and continuous improvement
* Cross-functional communication and collaboration

*The above is intended to outline the general content and requirements for this role and should not be considered an exhaustive list of duties, responsibilities, or physical demands. Nothing in this job posting limits management’s right to assign or reassign tasks as needed. Reasonable accommodations may be provided to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

*Mayzo is committed to a fair, merit-based hiring process. We use inclusive job postings, standardized evaluation criteria, and bias-awareness training for hiring managers. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process, and our practices are regularly reviewed to support equal opportunity and a respectful, harassment-free workplace.*

role.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
role.description:
The Howmet engines business produces world-class aerospace engine components, including investment castings, fasteners, rings and forgings. Our vacuum melted superalloys, machining, performance coatings and hot isostatic pressing for high performance parts enable the next generation of quieter, cleaner and more fuel-efficient aerospace engines. Able to supply more than 90% of structural and rotating aerospace engine components. 
 

Howmet Engines seeks an experienced professional to join our team! The **Continuous Improvement Director** at Howmet Aerospace is responsible for driving the implementation and sustained use of Lean principles, enhancing operational efficiency and fostering a culture of continuous improvement across the business segment This role serves as a teacher, coach and mentor, working closely with employees at all levels to build long-term adoption of CI practices. The Continuous Improvement Director partners with Senior Leadership to align improvement initiatives with business objectives, ensuring measurable impact on productivity, capacity and overall business segment performance.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Lead the continued development and enhancement of the Howmet Business System journey, including accelerating the Lean Execution Systems Assessment process and progress, working with plant teams on gap closure plans in support of advancing the CI culture across the business segment.
* Facilitate the Howmet Business System “HBS” journey best practice sharing within the location and across teams through a sustainable electronic system that allows users to search for common issues or problems.
* Lead OEE improvement actions deep dive with leaders and provide avenues for best practice sharing.
* Lead Howmet Business System implementation of continuous improvement initiatives and drive waste reductions utilizing Lean principles (JIT, Autonomation, Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, 5S, Standard Work, Line/Cell Design, Single Piece Flow, Material Flow, Visual Management, SMED, TPM, Root Cause Problem Solving, etc.)
* Facilitate Hoshins, Kaizens, problem solving, and rapid improvement process events with internal personnel at all levels of the organization, consultants, customers, and suppliers as needed. This includes providing support to sustain all follow-throughs required to sustain the improvements initiated during those events, especially those concentrated on local improvement.
* Understand and analyze Profit and Loss (P&L) statements to identify opportunities for cost reduction, revenue enhancement, and margin improvement. Lead and collaborate with cross functional internal teams focused on shop floor factory improvements, which could include CAPEX.
* Assist team leaders in team skill and knowledge development to support meeting management goals, project management, improvements, results measurements, problem solving and related team skills.
* Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to track progress and measure the impact of improvement initiatives.
* Drive change management efforts to ensure successful implementation and sustainability of process improvements.
* Identify and share best practices, lessons learned, and success stories to promote knowledge sharing and continuous learning within the organization.
* Provide coaching and mentorship to team members across the organization to drive the Continuous Improvement mindset.
* May participate or lead other targeted initiatives or kaizens as directed by the BU, as defined by the Segment Vice President.
* Role may support other sites’ continuous improvement activities, as needed (e.g., training, project-based work, best practice support, etc.)

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Minimum 10 years of experience in manufacturing environments in areas such as: Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, or Operational Excellence
* Minimum of 7 years in leadership roles in Operations or Continuous Improvement
* Previous experience in an aerospace, automotive or other manufacturing environment requiring significant lean strategies to maintain wins and propel the organizations’ success through Continuous Improvement
* Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited institution
* Must be willing to travel up to 50% of the time, including domestic and international travel
* Strong working knowledge and understanding of Continuous Process Improvement methodologies such as Lean and Six Sigma.
* Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
* This position is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) which requires U.S. person status. ITAR defines U.S. person as an U.S. Citizen, U.S. Permanent Resident (i.e. 'Green Card Holder'), Political Asylee, or Refugee
* Employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s Degree and Master's Degree from an accredited institution in Engineering or Supply Chain field of study highly desired
* Project Management certification or earned certificate
* Experience developing operations leadership development programs in a manufacturing environment
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing improvement techniques, including hoshin, flow principles, Jidoka, Kanban, 5S, and “plan for every part” (PFEP).
* Strong skills in value stream mapping and associated improvement methodologies.
* Understanding of pillars of Toyota production system (JIT, Jidoka).
* Experience evaluating TAKT time vs. cycle time, determining work area constraints (i.e. cycle time constraint, periodic work constraints, downtime constraints).
* Experience on the shop floor, working with employees, and enhancing manufacturing processes.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills require the ability to resolve conflicting interests and obtain cooperation.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills: able to develop and use structured approaches to identify root causes and recommend resolutions.
* Demonstrated experience in project leadership and project management skills, with ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously to meet objectives and key deadlines.

**Compensation and Benefits:**

If a pay range is identified for this job, it is based on a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. Actual compensation is subject to variation due to factors such as education, experience, skillset, market/business considerations, and/or location.

Howmet Aerospace offers a competitive benefits package to support the health, financial well-being, and professional growth of our employees. Benefits include:

* Comprehensive medical, prescription, dental, and vision benefits coverage, including FSA and HSA account options
* Pre-tax and Roth 401(k) retirement savings plans offering employer matching funds and a separate employer retirement contribution
* Paid holidays and vacation time (eligibility, accrual, and usage are discretionary and governed by applicable policies)
* Paid parental leave and adoption assistance programs
* Life insurance and disability coverage plans
* Optional coverage plans for auto, home, legal, identity theft, and pet insurance
* Tuition Assistance Program and ongoing professional development opportunities
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

**Our Story:**

Howmet Aerospace Inc. (NYSE: HWM), headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, is a leading global provider of advanced engineered solutions for the aerospace and transportation industries. Our primary businesses focus on jet engine components, aerospace fastening systems, titanium structural parts and forged wheels. With $8.3 Billion in revenue in 2025, our products play a crucial role in enabling fuel efficiency and lightweighting, contributing to our customers’ success and making a positive impact on the world. To learn more about the way Howmet Aerospace Inc. is advancing the sustainability of our customers, markets, and communities where we operate, review the 2025 Environmental Social and Governance report at www.howmet.com/esg-report. Follow: LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:**

Howmet is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Director, Global Training & Enablement is a strategic leader responsible for designing, building, and scaling a unified global training model that supports Direct Travel's "Everyone Is a VIP" operating vision. This role owns the end-to-end training function—from curriculum development through delivery, certification, and continuous improvement—ensuring advisors across all regions, service locations, and delivery partners deliver world-class service on the Avenir platform at enterprise scale.

This position blends strategic program ownership with hands-on team leadership, driving consistency, operational excellence, and measurable service impact across all geographies and service lines.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Global Training Strategy & Unified Model Leadership**

* Own and execute the **five-pillar global training model**: Unified Team, Unified Curriculum, Unified Intake, Unified Delivery, and Unified Tracking
* Establish and lead the **Global Enterprise Training Team (HUB)**, implementing a train-the-trainer model across all service locations and delivery teams
* Define and maintain **one mandatory core curriculum path** for every advisor role globally, with role-based elective catalogs
* Ensure training aligns with **COO strategic priorities**: "Everyone Is a VIP," margin expansion, and scalable service delivery without proportional headcount growth
* Build **Avenir platform-specific training** covering conversational booking, disruption management, trip queries, advisor-in-platform workflows, and exception management
* Create **global service standards** while enabling market-specific delivery and localization (language, currency, regulations, cultural nuance)

* **Training Team Leadership & Development**

* Lead, mentor, and develop a global team of **certified Enterprise Trainers** across multiple regions and time zones
* Establish and operationalize **trainer certification program** with recertification cycles tied to platform releases and curriculum updates
* Provide weekly team updates, performance feedback, and coaching on training effectiveness and learner outcomes
* Build **train-the-trainer capability** across all service locations to scale training delivery without proportional cost growth
* Establish a regular **trainer alignment cadence** across all locations to ensure consistency, share best practices, and cascade product/platform changes
* Hold trainers accountable to **learner feedback scores** and training effectiveness metrics

* **Avenir & Platform-Specific Curriculum Development**

* Design and maintain **Avenir-focused training modules** covering:
* + Agentic AI workflows and exception management
 + Conversational booking and trip management via chat, SMS, WhatsApp, and voice
 + Predictive disruption signals and proactive rebooking
 + Dynamic policy compliance and automated approvals
 + Profile depth and traveler intent anticipation
 + One-platform orchestration (air, hotel, rail, car, expense, payments, risk, comms)
* Create training for **AI-assisted tools and automation**
* Ensure advisors understand their role as **Experience Managers, not transaction processors**—focusing on exceptions, nuance, and high-value client interactions
* Develop **change management training** for platform releases, new AI capabilities, and policy/workflow updates

* **Service Delivery Model Enablement & Transition Readiness**

* Lead **onboarding readiness** for work transitions and service delivery model changes, ensuring advisors in all locations are equipped to handle Core, Avenir, and GDS servicing
* Develop **scalable, localized training** that maintains global standards while reflecting local market requirements, regulations, and cultural context
* Support **new market and location launches** with training frameworks adaptable across all regions and markets
* Partner with **Operations leadership** to align training timelines with capacity plans and work transition schedules
* Build **follow-the-sun training support** that scales with the service footprint, ensuring advisors in every time zone can access to learning resources and trainer guidance

* **Unified Intake, Delivery & Tracking**

* Establish **one standard global training request form** auto-routed to certified trainers with defined SLAs and lead times
* Implement **single global Learning Management System (LMS)** with real-time dashboards tracking:
* + Learner progress, compliance, and pass/fail reporting
 + Training completion and role-based certification status
 + Trainer effectiveness scored via learner feedback
 + Performance analytics linked to operational KPIs (SLA, quality, productivity)
* Design **multiple delivery modalities**: instructor-led, e-learning self-paced, job aids, workflow guides, and peer coaching
* Establish **standard global communication methods** (email, chat, escalations) for training support and change notifications
* Define **change management workflow** for curriculum updates, ensuring rapid deployment of product/platform changes

* **Measurement, Reporting & Continuous Improvement**

* Track and report **training effectiveness metrics** aligned to operational impact:
* + Advisor productivity and quality improvements post-training
 + SLA attainment and consistency across regions
 + AI tool adoption rates and workflow automation compliance
 + Learner satisfaction and trainer effectiveness scores
* Implement **post-training evaluations and performance assessments** to validate skill mastery and readiness
* Establish **continuous improvement cadence** (monthly) with Global Training Council to escalate insights, approve content changes, and refine delivery
* Publish **Year 1 capability report** to leadership demonstrating training ROI and operational impact
* Link training outcomes to **global talent development** and career progression

* **Cross-Functional Collaboration & Governance**

* Partner with **Efficiency & Operations teams** to translate workflow automation and AI initiatives into training content
* Collaborate with **Product teams** on Avenir training and platform readiness
* Align with **GDS, Core Product Support, and Avenir Product Support** teams on platform-specific curriculum
* Establish **Global Training Governance** with clear ownership, escalation paths, and decision rights
* Support **enterprise-wide transformation initiatives**, embedding training into PMO and change management workflows

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* **5+ years** in travel operations, training, workforce enablement, or related function
* **Proven experience managing a team of trainers or learning professionals** across multiple regions
* **Deep expertise in corporate travel operations**, GDS platforms (Sabre, Amadeus), and international ticketing
* **Demonstrated ability designing and scaling training programs** across geographies, cultures, and time zones
* **Strong communication and facilitation skills**; ability to simplify complex technical and operational topics
* **Global mindset and comfort working across time zones**, cultures, and organizational boundaries
* **Project management discipline** with ability to manage multiple workstreams and timelines simultaneously

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience with **multi-location or global service delivery models and distributed team leadership**
* **Hands-on knowledge of Avenir platform** or similar modern travel booking/servicing systems
* Background with **AI/automation tools** (including agentic AI platforms)
* Familiarity with **workflow automation** or **agent-assist technologies**
* **LMS implementation or administration** experience (configuration, reporting, user management)
* Experience in a **fast-paced, transformation-focused environment** with rapid platform/product evolution
* **Training ROI analysis** and ability to link learning outcomes to operational metrics

**SUCCESS MEASURES (FIRST 12–18 MONTHS)**

* **Global training framework** (five pillars) established, approved, and operationalized across Direct Travel and ATPI
* **Avenir platform training** fully developed and deployed; 90%+ advisor proficiency on core workflows
* **Global Enterprise Training Team (HUB)** stood up with certified trainers across regions; train-the-trainer model active
* **Onboarding readiness** achieved; service delivery and work transitions supported with zero training-readiness gaps
* **Single global LMS** live with real-time dashboards; 100% training compliance tracking across all advisors
* **Unified intake process** live; training SLAs met with <5% variance across regions
* **Advisor productivity and quality improvements** measurable post-training (target: 10–15% efficiency gain, consistent SLA attainment)
* **AI tool adoption** at 80%+ usage rates
* **Trainer effectiveness scores** averaging 4.2+/5.0 on learner feedback; continuous improvement cadence established
* **New market and location launch training** embedded in operational rhythm across all regions

**ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS**

* **Willing to travel 15–25%** as needed to support service locations and global training initiatives
* **Flexibility to work across time zones** for trainer alignment calls, global stand-ups, and 24/7 training support model
* **Comfort with ambiguity and rapid change** in a transformation-focused environment

**Design. Disrupt. Repeat.**

Be an agent of change on a team committed to achieving client-focused, mission-driven excellence. Steampunk is looking for an experienced Director of Operations with an appetite for taking on new challenges.

**Why Steampunk?**

Our people are the very core of what we do; their expertise and hunger for new and exciting challenges fuel our relentless pursuit of mission success. role.description:
**About Lyra Health** 
Lyra Health is a leading provider of evidence-based mental health care, serving more than 20 million people globally in partnership with employers and more than 100 million through health plan and partner relationships. The company has delivered more than 15 million sessions of mental health care, published more than 35 peer-reviewed studies, and delivered unmatched outcomes in terms of access, clinical effectiveness, and cost efficiency. Extensive peer-reviewed research confirms Lyra’s transformative care model helps people recover twice as fast and results in a 26% annual reduction in overall healthcare claims costs. Lyra is transforming access to life-changing mental health care through Lyra Empower, the only fully integrated, AI-powered platform combining the highest-quality care and technology solutions.

**About The Role**

We are seeking a **Senior Director, Enterprise Operations** to drive a step-function improvement in Lyra’s internal operating leverage and effectiveness. Reporting to the Chief Clinical Operations Officer and working in close partnership with the Chief Information Officer, you will build and execute an enterprise-wide strategy aimed to transform our operating cadence, optimize operational efficiency, and embed AI-driven workflows across all core business functions.

**What You’ll Do:**

* Define Lyra’s multi-year enterprise transformation strategy, prioritizing high-impact initiatives that transform Lyra’s pace of delivery and optimize our internal operations

* Drive forward Lyra’s enterprise transformation roadmap, taking cross-functional projects from concept to measurable operational outcome

* Establish transformation KPIs (e.g., productivity lift, cost-to-serve reduction, throughput velocity) and track realized ROI against Finance benchmarks

* Proactively identify key blockers towards success and identify investments required to accelerate impact

* Lead a cross-functional team of strategic operators to drive forward operational transformation projects and partner closely with our dedicated technical teams to bring the technical initiatives to life

* Enable a high-performing work culture oriented towards ongoing operational excellence and AI fluency

**Requirements:**

* **Leadership Experience:** 15+ years of overall business experience, including 8+ years leading large-scale operational or digital transformations at growth-stage or enterprise tech companies

* **Organizational and Process Redesign:** Proven experience identifying key blockers to organizational effectiveness, scoping out potential paths forward, building alignment on the solution, and executing

* **AI & Tech Capabilities:** Proven track record deploying enterprise AI solutions, automation workflows, and/or advanced analytics to drive operating leverage

* **Financial & Analytical Rigor:** Deep expertise in financial modeling, business case development, and tracking post-implementation ROI alongside Finance

* **Change Management:** Demonstrated success leading cross-functional teams through complex organizational and workflow shifts.

* **Leadership Approach:** Strategic executor who thrives in fast-paced, high-growth, and ambiguous environments and is an effective communicator across organizations

As a full-time Senior Director, Enterprise Operations, you will be employed by Lyra Health, Inc. The anticipated annual base salary range for this full-time position is $211,000 to $265,000. The base range is determined by role and level, and placement within the range will depend on a number of job-related factors, including but not limited to your skills, qualifications, experience and location. This role may also be eligible for discretionary bonuses.

Annual salary is only one part of an employee’s total compensation package at Lyra. We also offer generous benefits that include:

* Comprehensive healthcare coverage (including medical, dental, vision, FSA/HSA, life and disability insurances)

* Lyra for Lyrians; coaching and therapy services

* Equity in the company through discretionary restricted stock units

* Competitive time off with pay policies including vacation, sick days, and company holidays

* Paid parental leave

* 401K retirement benefits

* Monthly tech allowance

* We like to spread joy throughout the year with well-being perks and activities, surprise swag, regular community celebration…and more!

We can’t wait to meet you.

role.title: Director of Integration & Operational Excellence
role.description:
We're Scan.com. We're building America's national imaging network: the infrastructure that connects patients, providers, and payers to faster, better-value diagnostic imaging. Thousands of patients move through our platform every day, and each is a real person waiting for an answer to a healthcare concern. We exist to get them that answer faster.

We manage the medical imaging pathway end-to-end. Providers order through a single point of entry, and from there, we run the entire medical diagnostic pathway. Managing the full pathway, rather than brokering pieces of it, is what lets us deliver imaging faster, at higher quality, and at a lower cost than the fragmented status quo.

We're looking for a **Director of Integration & Operational Excellence** at an exciting time. We've raised over $200m in funding to date, reached profitability, and are growing 100% year on year.

Millions of people wait too long for a diagnosis. Come help us fix that.

**WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE IN THIS ROLE**
--------------------------------------

You'll report to our Chief Operating Officer and Co-Founder and work closely with the CEO, Corporate Development, our CFO and leaders across Operations, Commercial, Product, Technology, People and Clinical. Your mandate is to make acquisitions work in practice and build the operating capability that allows Scan.com to integrate businesses repeatedly as we grow.

You'll join before upcoming acquisitions close, learn how Scan.com operates, and help prepare both our business and acquired teams for integration. You'll own the integrated plan, budget, dependencies, and delivery cadence from operational diligence through Day 1, the first 100 days, and the handover to business-as-usual owners. Functional leaders retain accountability for decisions in their areas; you'll hold the overall plan together, drive execution, and bring unresolved trade-offs to the COO.

Success means retained customers and referral relationships, uninterrupted patient service, reliable billing and collections, and measurable improvements in operating performance.

* **Lead integration planning before close.** Work with Corporate Development and Finance to test the operating assumptions behind each acquisition, identify integration costs and working-capital needs, and turn diligence findings into a practical delivery plan.
* **Build the integration playbook.** Establish Day 1 readiness criteria, 100-day plans, workstream owners, decision rights, budgets, and escalation routes. Adapt the approach to founder-owned businesses, carve-outs, referral networks and imaging centers.
* **Prepare** **Scan.com** **to receive acquired businesses.** Identify capacity constraints in scheduling, billing, customer support, technology and management. Resolve gaps before moving additional volume onto our platform.
* **Own execution across workstreams.** Lead the integration cadence across Finance, Operations, Commercial, People, Product, Technology and Clinical, working with Legal and Compliance on the approvals needed in their areas. Sequence concurrent integrations around available capacity.
* **Protect the business through change.** Build relationships with acquired founders and teams, identify key people and customer relationships to retain, and coordinate clear communications and responsibilities.
* **Make systems and process changes work operationally.** Partner with technical and operational owners on referral routing, scheduling, imaging systems, reporting and billing migrations. Agree testing, reconciliation, cutover criteria and contingency plans before switching.
* **Deliver the financial case.** Establish baselines with Finance and track revenue retention, collections, operating costs, and realized synergies. Separate one-time integration costs from recurring benefits and avoid counting growth or savings already included in the plan.
* **Improve operating performance across** **Scan.com****.** Lead focused projects on center and mobile-unit economics, staffing, vendor costs, workflows and capacity. Build the business case, implement the changes, and demonstrate the result in operating metrics and the P&L.
* **Build a practical operating cadence.** Maintain a reliable view of owners, milestones, budgets, risks, and decisions. Use automation and AI to reduce reporting work and give leadership concise updates on what needs attention.
* **Make improvements stick.** Document repeatable processes, train the teams who will run them, and hand over completed workstreams with clear ownership and measures of success.

**Example projects**

* Prepare a founder-owned imaging business for Day 1, retaining key relationships while aligning financial reporting and collections.
* Build a carve-out plan that identifies essential staff, systems and shared services, with costed transitional arrangements and clear exit dates.
* Validate referral-level unit economics and center capacity before moving new patient volume onto Scan.com's network.
* Reconcile an acquired company's billing and receivables data, establish collection baselines and resolve issues before a systems migration.

**YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS**
----------------------

Your ramp begins inside Scan.com, before an acquisition closes. The timing of live integrations will depend on the deal pipeline; preparation and operating improvement start immediately.

* **Days 1–30: learn the business at ground level.** Spend time with scheduling, center operations, Commercial, Finance, and revenue-cycle teams. Follow cases from referral through scan, report, billing, and payment. Review prior integrations, map the core systems and handoffs, and establish baseline service and financial metrics.
* **Days 31–60: build readiness.** Assess upcoming acquisitions alongside the deal team. Identify receiving-team capacity constraints, retention risks, and operational dependencies. Produce costed Day 1 and 100-day plans with named owners, and deliver an initial improvement to an existing Scan.com workflow.
* **Days 61–90: test and lead delivery.** Rehearse critical workflows and agree readiness criteria with functional owners. Launch the integration reporting cadence and lead the first implementation workstreams as transactions permit. Give leadership a clear view of what is ready, what needs fixing, and what should be sequenced later.

**How we'll measure success**

* Customer, referral volume, and key-employee retention.
* Patient access, scheduling performance and report turnaround through transitions.
* Billing accuracy, cash collections and receivables performance.
* Realized margin improvement and synergies, validated with Finance and measured against integration costs.
* Delivery against agreed budgets and milestones, followed by a successful handover to operational owners.

**WHAT YOU MIGHT BRING TO THE TABLE**
-------------------------------------

You don't need to meet every criterion. We are looking for someone who has personally led acquisitions through operational integration and can show what changed after close.

* **A record of delivering integrations.** You've led multiple post-acquisition integrations or substantial workstreams with direct accountability for outcomes. You can explain what went wrong, how you responded, and what the financial and operational results were.
* **Healthcare operating experience.** You've worked in a multisite healthcare, diagnostic imaging, healthcare-services, or similarly complex operating business. Experience in a PE-backed platform, founder-owned acquisition, or carve-out is particularly relevant.
* **Operational and financial depth.** You've owned a P&L, an operating function, or an integration programme with measurable financial responsibility. You can connect staffing, capacity, pricing, service quality, and collections to profitability and cash flow.
* **Understanding of the revenue cycle.** You understand how provider contracts, credentialing, billing workflows, denials, and receivables affect delivery and cash. Imaging-specific experience is valuable.
* **Experience implementing change.** You've worked with technical and operational teams on systems migrations, process standardization, or service transitions, including testing and reconciliation.
* **Credibility with acquired teams.** You can earn the trust of founders and frontline staff, retain what makes a business successful and make difficult changes clearly and respectfully.
* **Strong financial and analytical judgment.** You can build and challenge unit economics, integration budgets and business cases, distinguish recurring benefits from one-off effects, and investigate the detail behind a misleading headline metric.
* **Leadership across functions.** You establish clear accountability, resolve competing priorities and escalate decisions early. You are comfortable holding senior stakeholders to commitments.
* **A hands-on approach.** You're willing to spend time in centers and alongside operating teams, investigate individual cases and improve processes before they are fully documented. The role involves travel to Scan.com operations and acquired businesses.
* **Practical use of AI and automation.** You improve how work gets done while keeping appropriate human review over sensitive data, financial decisions, and operational changes.

Experience in consulting, transaction services, or strategic finance can be valuable when combined with direct responsibility for implementation and results after close.

**AI REQUIREMENTS**
-------------------

At Scan.com, AI isn't a side project; it's how we work. We expect everyone to use AI to think faster, remove drudgery, and multiply their output. What we care about is judgment: knowing when AI makes you sharper, when it doesn't, and how to use it responsibly around patient data. We'll assess this in the way that matters for this role, using the tier below. You don't need to be an engineer. You need to reach for the best tool and get more done as a result.

* Tier 1 — For this role, the expectation is that you are an AI-Native. You build with AI directly, shipping, automating, or prototyping real work with LLMs and agents, and have clear judgment on where humans must stay in the loop.

 + You build with AI, not just alongside it. You've shipped, automated, or prototyped something real using LLMs, agents, or AI tooling.
 + You can explain a workflow you redesigned so a machine does the boring 80%.
 + You have a view on where agentic systems help and where a human must stay in the loop, especially in regulated, PHI-adjacent work.
 + **Assessment:** a practical exercise where you use AI tools live or in a take-home.

**A VIEW ON OUR CULTURE**
-------------------------

We're building something that matters. Every scan we speed up is a real person waiting on an answer, and that urgency runs through everything we do. We move fast, we own outcomes, and take pride in our output. If you like ambiguity, working with ambitious people, and want your work to visibly move the needle, you'll feel at home here.

**HOW WE WILL INTERVIEW YOU**
-----------------------------

We keep our interview process short and sweet. Here are the stages you can expect, but we might switch up the order depending on team availability:

* 30-minute introductory phone call with a member of our Talent Team.
* A 45-minute discussion with the COO covering integrations you've led, the operating decisions you owned, and the results you delivered.
* A practical integration case and 'Scan Standard' interview. You'll assess a fictional acquisition, identify the key risks and build a prioritized Day 1 and 100-day plan. We'll discuss how you would protect service and collections, measure success, and use AI tools in your work.
* Meet the founders and/or other team members. Again, the length varies depending on how many people are involved and whether in person or via video call.
* Offer!

**WHAT WE OFFER**
-----------------

We go beyond the basics with our benefits package. We believe great work starts with supporting our people. Here's what you can expect from us:

* Salary range of **$150,000 - $175,000**
* Equity
* Flexible remote or hybrid work options
* Dedicated personal development budget
* Medical, vision, and dental coverage
* 28+ days of paid time off across PTO and wellbeing days, so you can show up at your best
* Paid parental leave
* 401k retirement plan
* All the equipment you need to do your best work
* Inclusive, people-first policies designed by our team, for our team

**DIVERSITY AT** **SCAN.COM**
-----------------------------

Scan.com is committed to eliminating discrimination and encouraging diversity within our team. We strive to provide equality and fairness for all job applicants and employees and never discriminate on the basis of gender, marital status, age, race, ethnicity, religion, or physical differences.

We are opposed to all forms of unlawful treatment and discrimination.

Our ambition is for our team to be representative of society's diversity, and for every employee to feel respected and able to bring their best selves to work.

If you need an accommodation to apply or interview, contact us at people@scan.com.

We look forward to receiving your application!

United States - Remote

JOB ID: R-259392 LOCATION: United States - Remote WORK LOCATION TYPE: Remote DATE POSTED: Nov. 02, 2026 CATEGORY: Clinical SALARY RANGE: -

**Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients**
--------------------------------------------

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

 
 
 

**Local Study Operations Manager (LSOM), Director**
---------------------------------------------------

**What you will do**
--------------------

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will provide strategic and operational leadership for the country LSOM organization and is accountable for the quality, timeliness, cost, and compliant execution of the country clinical study portfolio. The role achieves results through LSOM Senior Managers and their FTE and FSP teams, translating global clinical development strategy into country operating priorities. The role directs portfolio delivery, resource and capacity strategy, financial planning, quality and risk management, vendor performance, and inspection readiness from feasibility through study close-out. As a member of the country leadership team, this role influences study placement and portfolio decisions, leads the resolution of significant operational issues, develops organizational capability and succession plans, and represents LSOM operations in country, regional, and global governance forums.

 
 

**Accountabilities**

* Lead the successful delivery of the country study portfolio through the LSOM management organization, ensuring alignment with global clinical development priorities.

* Provides strategic direction and leadership to LSOM country organization across the full study lifecycle, including feasibility, study execution, and study close-out.

* Establishes portfolio-level oversight of delivery, quality, risk, timelines, and performance, directing timely escalation and resolution of critical issues for LSOM management organization.

* Manage LSOM and LSOM vendor performance to guarantee high-quality study execution, serving as the primary escalation point for local study challenges, driving solutions, and ensuring portfolio targets are met within the country.

* Build leadership capability within the LSOM organization through targeted coaching, development, and succession planning, preparing LSOMs to lead increasingly complex trials and programs.

* Establishes strong operating partnerships with Clinical Research Associate (CRA) organization to support study start-up, monitoring, issue resolution, and compliant trial execution across the country portfolio.

* Cultivate a high-performing, accountable, and inclusive organization focused on operational excellence and continuous improvement.

* Champion strong integration between study strategy and local execution teams to translate portfolio priorities into effective country-level delivery.

* Strengthen cross-functional alignment and accountability across country teams to accelerate execution and deliver portfolio commitments.

* Influences study-placement and portfolio investment decisions by providing strategic insight into country's capabilities, operational readiness, performance, and growth potential.

* Anticipates portfolio-level delivery risks, quality trends, and evolving resource requirements, directing mitigation strategies and systemic improvements across country operations.

* Sponsor initiatives that advance operational efficiency, digital innovation, organizational capability, and the adoption of leading practices.

* Direct resource strategy, capacity planning, and workload allocation across FSP and FTE LSOM teams to optimize execution and align resources with global priorities.

* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, GCP, ICH, and organizational standards across the country's study portfolio.

Partner with the Regional Head/Country Head and senior cross-functional stakeholders to align priorities, establish accountability for trial deliverables, and resolve significant escalations. 



**Responsibilities**

* Serve as the functional leader for LSOM Senior Managers and the broader LSOM team, including both FSP and FTE, to optimize trial execution and align with global priorities. including strategy and execution, managing risks and escalations

* Partners closely with CRAs, CSPO, Quality, and FSP partners.

* Leads the coordination among country functional teams to ensure successful delivery of the country portfolio.

* Ensure inspection readiness and provide hands-on support during inspections, including responsibility for storyboards.

* Sponsors continuous operational improvement initiatives and encourage sharing of best practices.

* Ensure compliance with relevant regulatory and quality standards.

* Collaborate with the Regional Head/Country Head to engage cross-functional stakeholders, align on trial deliverables, and manage escalations as needed.

**Capability Building and People Leadership**

* Lead, coach, and develop LSOM Sr Managers, including performance management, succession planning, and leadership bench development.

* Build the organizational capabilities, resourcing needed to meet the current and future regional portfolio requirements.

* Foster a high-performing, inclusive, accountable, and patient-focused culture across geographically distributed teams.

* Lead organizational changes and enable adoption of new operating models, technologies

**Authority**

* Accountable for country level oversight and delivery of clinical trials.

* Manage the performance of LSOM Senior Managers and their teams

* Holds line management authority for regional and country operations leaders, including performance management, talent development, succession planning, and capability building.

* Sets regional delivery goals, operating expectations, and performance standards across study start-up, site engagement, monitoring, execution, and closeout.

* Capability build, talent and performance management, and acting as a liaison for cultural differences within region.

**Outputs**

* Manage LSOM resources in accordance with the global study strategy.

* Oversee resource allocation and workload balance across LSOMs.

* Handle FSP supplier resource coordination and monitor performance through quality oversight metrics.

* Identify and report any risks or compliance concerns related to FSP activities.

* Escalate issues to the Regional/Country Head as necessary.

**What we expect of you**

 
 

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Doctorate degree and 4 years of clinical research experience OR
* Master’s degree and 7 years of clinical research experience OR
* Bachelor’s degree and 9 years of clinical research experience

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* 4 years of direct managerial and/or leadership experience or equivalent

* Deep knowledge of ICH GCP, ICH E6(R3), ICH E8(R1), and global regulatory expectations for risk-based monitoring and clinical trial oversight.

* Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and lead complex cross-functional initiatives within a global matrix organization

* Strong Project Management experience

* Experience managing multiple teams / direct reports across multiple clinical functions / trials

* Experience at, or oversight of, clinical research vendors (CROs, central labs, imaging vendors, etc.)

* Experience managing clinical operations across relevant geography / region, including strong understanding of local regulatory requirements around global clinical trials

**What you can expect of us**
-----------------------------

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

Base Salary Range: $195,876-265,008

 
 

In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

* A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan
* Stock-based long-term incentives

role.title: Sr. Director, Launch Excellence & Operations
role.description:
***Join Immatics and shape the future of cancer immunotherapy; one patient at a time!***

Immatics is committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of patients with cancer. We are the global leader in precision targeting of **PRAME**, a target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Our cutting-edge science and robust clinical pipeline form the broadest **PRAME** franchise with the most **PRAME** indications and modalities, spanning TCR T-cell therapies and TCR bispecifics.

**Why Join Us?**

* **Innovative Environment:** Help to pioneer advancements in cancer immunotherapy.
* **Collaborative Culture:** Be part of a diverse team dedicated to your professional growth.
* **Global Impact:** Contribute to therapies that make a lasting impact on patients globally.

**Role Overview**

The Senior Director, Launch Excellence & Operations serves as a strategic partner and deputy to the VP, Launch Excellence, Strategy & Operations, helping shape and execute Immatics' commercial launch strategy. This highly visible role sits at the center of launch planning, governance, and operational readiness, ensuring cross-functional alignment and execution as the organization prepares for commercialization.

The successful candidate will lead integrated launch planning, support the Launch Readiness Review (LRR) process, and establish the operating rhythms, governance, and performance management frameworks necessary to drive launch success. This individual will operate seamlessly between strategy and execution, translating insights into action, guiding critical business decisions, and creating clarity in a dynamic and evolving environment.

**Reports to:** Vice President, Launch Excellence, Strategy & Operations

**Location:** US, Fully Remote

**Salary Range:** $250,000 - $290,000

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, business, engineering, or a related field with 15+ years of relevant experience OR
* MBA / advanced degree (MBA, PhD, MD, or equivalent) with 12+ years of relevant experience A combination of top-tier strategy consulting experience and in-house biopharmaceutical commercial strategy, commercial operations, or launch leadership experience.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* 5+ years in oncology; direct experience with TCR, CAR-T, or TIL cell therapies, including a first wave of commercial launch strongly preferred
* Demonstrated ownership of commercial launch strategy or launch readiness — including launch planning, cross-functional governance, milestone and risk management, and readiness tracking through to launch.
* Knowledge of personalized manufacturing and vein-to-vein logistics, including manufacturing slot allocation and patient journey management.
* Understanding of the melanoma treatment landscape, therapeutic decision-making, and patient access barriers.
* Working knowledge of the cell therapy operational value chain — treatment center authorization, apheresis scheduling, chain of identity / chain of custody, and product delivery.
* Experience standing up launch governance, a launch readiness review process, or a commercial PMO from scratch.
* Familiarity with digital launch excellence tools and analytics.
* Experience scoping and managing external consultants, agencies, and analytics vendors.
* Proven ability to drive strategic decision-making across functions without direct authority: framing the decision, assembling the analysis, aligning stakeholders, and driving the issue to closure.
* Exceptional executive communication, influencing, and synthesis skills; able to distill complex, ambiguous cross-functional situations into a clear recommendation
* Strong strategic planning and operational execution skills.

**In this role you will:**

**Launch Strategy & Commercial Planning**

* Partner with the VP to develop and execute an integrated launch strategy, roadmap, and commercial playbook.
* Lead strategic evaluations and business cases for critical commercial decisions, capabilities, and growth opportunities.
* Continuously refine launch strategy based on market, competitive, regulatory, and operational insights.
* Develop executive recommendations and materials for senior leadership and key governance forums.

**Launch Governance & Cross-Functional Integration**

* Drive cross-functional alignment, decision-making, and accountability through the Launch Readiness Review (LRR) process.
* Co-own launch readiness planning, including critical milestones, dependencies, risks, and mitigation strategies.
* Establish and maintain operating rhythms, governance processes, and communication forums that support launch execution.
* Facilitate resolution of complex cross-functional issues and ensure timely escalation of key decisions.

**Operational Readiness & Cell Therapy Operations Performance**

* Build and monitor performance frameworks across the end-to-end cell therapy patient journey.
* Partner with operational teams to identify and address patient funnel attrition, process bottlenecks, and execution risks.
* Provide commercial leadership for systems, analytics, and reporting capabilities that enable launch readiness and operational excellence.
* Develop scalable processes and performance metrics to support successful commercialization.

**Travel Requirements:**

* Up to 20% travel to support cross-functional team meetings, treatment center engagement, advisory boards, congresses, and launch activities, including periodic travel to Immatics US in Stafford, TX

Qualified candidates will participate in a structured interview process, which includes:

* An initial recruiter phone screen (conducted via video)
* Interviews with the hiring leader and other key stakeholders (via video)
* A final-stage interview

**What do we offer?**

At Immatics, we believe in investing in our team’s health, safety and well-being. Here’s what you can expect if you join Immatics

**Comprehensive Benefits**:

* Competitive rates for Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
* 4 weeks of vacation, granted up front each year and prorated for first and last year of employment.
* 12 company paid holidays
* 7 days of sick time
* 100% employer-paid life insurance up to at 1x annual salary, up to one hundred thousand dollars
* 100% employer-paid short- and long-Term disability coverage
* 401(k) with immediate eligibility and company match. The company will match 100% of your contributions up to 3% of your base salary for the first two years of employment, 4% for years 2-3 of employment, and up to 5% of your salary from the fourth year onward of continued employment.
* Partially paid parental leave for eligible employees.
* Additional voluntary employee-paid benefits and services, including accident, hospital indemnity, and critical illness insurance, as well as identity theft protection and pet insurance.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

**Reasonable Accommodations**

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and to applicants with sincerely held religious beliefs, practices, or observances. If you require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at RecruitingUS@immatics.com.

**Work Authorization**

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future sponsorship.

**Pre-Employment Requirements**

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, reference checks and pre-employment drug screening, where permitted by applicable law. For certain roles, additional screenings such as a credit check or motor vehicle record review may be required, where job-related and consistent with business necessity.

**Notice to Staffing Agencies and Third-Party Recruiters**

Immatics US partners with a select group of approved staffing agencies. Candidate submissions are accepted only from agencies that have a current written agreement with Immatics US and signed and formally engaged by our Talent Acquisition team for an active search. Unsolicited resumes or candidate information, including submissions made directly to hiring managers, will not be considered and are not eligible for placement fees.

Description Director of Operations - Hybrid

**Role Overview:**

We are seeking a high-caliber, transformative **Director of Operations** to lead, scale, and optimize our operations. In this role, you will serve as a strategic leader responsible for driving operational excellence, customer advocacy, and regulatory integrity across a multi-faceted organization.

 
 

You will move beyond routine contact center management to steer a dynamic organization comprised of specialized internal operational teams—covering strategic readiness, advanced customer advocacy, and complex fraud/escalation management—alongside large-scale BPO vendor partners managing ~200+ frontline agents.

 
 

You bring a blend of strategic vision, process optimization discipline, vendor governance, and high-impact people leadership required to elevate operational standards and deliver best-in-class customer experiences.

 
 

**You have a proven track record of:**

* **Large-Scale Operations Leadership**: Successfully leading multi-site contact center operations combining internal teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners of 200+ headcount.
* **Operational Transformation**: Transforming reactive service centers into proactive, quality-focused customer advocacy hubs through structured process engineering.
* **Escalation & Fraud Management**: Effectively mitigating enterprise risk through robust Tier 2 & 3 complaint handling, fraud prevention protocols, and regulatory adherence.
* **Vendor Operations Governance**: Driving rigorous SLA performance, cost efficiency, and quality alignment across third-party BPO vendor organizations.
 

 

**What you’ll do:**

The Director of Operations maintains end-to-end accountability for operational strategy, performance delivery, vendor oversight, and organizational readiness.

* **Leadership Reach**: Direct oversight of Department Managers, Unit Managers (UMs), and Vendor Managers (VMs) across internal and external business units.
* **Core Internal Operations**:
 + **Strategic Operations:** Driving CX quality call listening, 1:1 and group coaching/training, operations readiness, and training materials maintenance.
 + **Customer Advocacy:** Overseeing high-touch inbound customer service, task execution, complex account resolution, and U.S. transfer handling.
 + **Escalations and Fraud**: Leading high-severity escalated problem solving, fraud operations, customer complaint research and resolution, and escalation follow-ups.
* **Core External Operations:**
 + Governance and SLA performance tracking for primary vendor partners overseeing a network of ~200+ non-associate vendor agents performing inbound calls and funding workflows.

 

**Key Focus Areas:**

* Reimagine end to end Operations in this era of AI
* Strategic Leadership & Governance to formulate and execute long-term operational strategies and partner cross functionally
* Partner cross-functionally with Product, Business Analysis, and Process teams to establish and update processes, policies, procedures, and standards
* Define operational KPIs, quality targets, and SLA metrics to ensure consistent service delivery, funding accuracy, and customer satisfaction
* Direct vendor management leads to oversee third-party partners, ensuring ~200+ vendor agents adhere to operational guidelines and productivity benchmarks
* Risk, Fraud, & Complaint Resolution spanning complex problem solving and root-cause analysis
* Ensure business readiness for product launches, process updates, and technology enhancements across all operational sub-functions
* Mentor, develop, and inspire a multi-layered leadership team, cultivating a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and high performance.
* Optimize talent allocation and capacity planning across teams to handle volume fluctuations dynamically.
 

 

**Location:** Plano, TX - This role is designated as a hybrid position. You are expected to adhere to Capital One's hybrid policy regarding required on-site presence at your designated office location.

 
 

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree or military experience
* At least 5 years of people leadership experience
* At least 5 years of process or project management experience
* At least 5 years of relationship management experience
* At least 5 years of experience delivering transformational initiatives
 

 

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* PMP, Lean, Agile, or Six Sigma certification
* At least 3 years of operations people leadership experience
* At least 7 years of people leadership experience
