Director of Operations - Hybrid

**Role Overview:**

We are seeking a high-caliber, transformative **Director of Operations** to lead, scale, and optimize our operations. In this role, you will serve as a strategic leader responsible for driving operational excellence, customer advocacy, and regulatory integrity across a multi-faceted organization.

You will move beyond routine contact center management to steer a dynamic organization comprised of specialized internal operational teams—covering strategic readiness, advanced customer advocacy, and complex fraud/escalation management—alongside large-scale BPO vendor partners managing ~200+ frontline agents.

You bring a blend of strategic vision, process optimization discipline, vendor governance, and high-impact people leadership required to elevate operational standards and deliver best-in-class customer experiences.

**You have a proven track record of:**

* **Large-Scale Operations Leadership**: Successfully leading multi-site contact center operations combining internal teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners of 200+ headcount.
* **Operational Transformation**: Transforming reactive service centers into proactive, quality-focused customer advocacy hubs through structured process engineering.
* **Escalation & Fraud Management**: Effectively mitigating enterprise risk through robust Tier 2 & 3 complaint handling, fraud prevention protocols, and regulatory adherence.
* **Vendor Operations Governance**: Driving rigorous SLA performance, cost efficiency, and quality alignment across third-party BPO vendor organizations.

**What you’ll do:**

The Director of Operations maintains end-to-end accountability for operational strategy, performance delivery, vendor oversight, and organizational readiness.

* **Leadership Reach**: Direct oversight of Department Managers, Unit Managers (UMs), and Vendor Managers (VMs) across internal and external business units.
* **Core Internal Operations**:
 + **Strategic Operations:** Driving CX quality call listening, 1:1 and group coaching/training, operations readiness, and training materials maintenance.
 + **Customer Advocacy:** Overseeing high-touch inbound customer service, task execution, complex account resolution, and U.S. transfer handling.
 + **Escalations and Fraud**: Leading high-severity escalated problem solving, fraud operations, customer complaint research and resolution, and escalation follow-ups.
* **Core External Operations:**
 + Governance and SLA performance tracking for primary vendor partners overseeing a network of ~200+ non-associate vendor agents performing inbound calls and funding workflows.

**Key Focus Areas:**

* Reimagine end to end Operations in this era of AI
* Strategic Leadership & Governance to formulate and execute long-term operational strategies and partner cross functionally
* Partner cross-functionally with Product, Business Analysis, and Process teams to establish and update processes, policies, procedures, and standards
* Define operational KPIs, quality targets, and SLA metrics to ensure consistent service delivery, funding accuracy, and customer satisfaction
* Direct vendor management leads to oversee third-party partners, ensuring ~200+ vendor agents adhere to operational guidelines and productivity benchmarks
* Risk, Fraud, & Complaint Resolution spanning complex problem solving and root-cause analysis
* Ensure business readiness for product launches, process updates, and technology enhancements across all operational sub-functions
* Mentor, develop, and inspire a multi-layered leadership team, cultivating a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and high performance.
* Optimize talent allocation and capacity planning across teams to handle volume fluctuations dynamically.

role.description:
**Job Description**

**This role is fully remote and must be located within the 50 U.S. states. Standard working hours are in Eastern Timezone. Semi-annual travel may be required to a Devoted office for on-site work.**

**A bit about this role:**

At Devoted, our mission is to dramatically improve the health and well-being of our members by treating each of them like family. Devoted is growing at an incredible pace, and we are thrilled to welcome and serve every new member who joins us. This growth demands that our Utilization Management (UM) operation must scale and evolve without ever losing sight of the people at the center of every authorization.

We believe UM done right means decisions that are correct, fair, and fast, delivered through a frictionless process and with heart. Behind every request is a member waiting on care and a provider working to deliver it. UM is hard, but the challenge doesn’t exempt us from our mission.

We are seeking a curious, operationally minded leader to serve as Director, Utilization Management Operations. Reporting to the Vice President of Health Services, you will lead the teams behind our administrative work: a large onshore and offshore team of UM Administrative Coordinators who manage intake, outreach, notifications, and follow-up. You will also hold dotted-line accountability for monitoring and ensuring the success of our Part B medical authorization turnaround times (TAT).

This role is for someone who is energized by a complex process: someone who wants to unravel it, reimagine it, and lead the build of something simpler, faster, and more consistent. You will have significant influence over the roadmap for Orinoco, our internal technology platform, and an integrated AI engine to put to work. This role will help pave the way towards realizing the next generation of our UM program, driving improvements in effectiveness, efficiency, and experience for our members and provider partners.

**Your Responsibilities and Impact will include**:

* **SLA & Timeliness Ownership:** Own SLA performance for the administrative steps that support authorization review across UM, delivering consistent, predictable performance at a meaningfully lower cost. Hold dotted-line accountability for Part B medical authorization turnaround times (TAT), partnering with the clinical leaders of that team to monitor performance, surface risks early, and remove administrative barriers to on-time decisions.
* **Process Reimagination:** Map our administrative processes end to end, including auth intake, requests for additional clinical information, facility census checks, member and provider notifications, and member follow-up, and lead their redesign for speed, consistency, and simplicity.
* **Technology & AI Leadership:** Partner with Product and Engineering to shape the Orinoco roadmap so that process and technology evolve together. Put our integrated AI tools to work to remove manual effort, so our administrative capacity no longer has to grow at the same rate as our membership.
* **Build for Measurement:** Design processes that are highly measurable and transparent by default. Partner with Data Science to define and monitor the KPIs that matter, including timeliness, cost per authorization, quality, and provider experience, and use them to drive decisions and continuous improvement.
* **People & Vendor Leadership:** Lead and develop a team that includes approximately 50 onshore UM Administrative Coordinators and their leaders. Manage our offshore vendor partnership, which supports more than 250 administrative team members, holding it to clear performance standards while building a shared culture of ownership and care.
* **Provider & Member Experience:** Partner with the Provider Network team to understand what providers and facilities need from this process, and build it in. Design every touchpoint, from outreach to notifications to follow-up, with the humans on the other end in mind.
* **Cross-Functional Partnership:** Work closely with the Senior Director of UM, who owns end-to-end authorization performance, along with the UM Medical Directors, Compliance, Provider Network, Data Science, and Engineering teams to keep the operation aligned and consistently audit-ready.

**Required skills and experience:**

* **Mission & Heart:** A genuine commitment to treating members like family, and a belief that operational excellence and empathy belong together.
* **Proven Operator at Scale:** A track record of leading high-volume operations that deliver consistent SLA performance.
* **Builder Mindset:** Experience taking a complex, multi-step process apart and leading the build of a simpler, more scalable one, rather than only maintaining what exists. You are naturally curious and ask why a step exists before deciding how to improve it.
* **Metrics-Oriented:** You build for measurement, are comfortable working deep in the workflows and the data, and use both to drive decisions and hold teams and partners accountable.
* **Technology & AI Curiosity:** Experience partnering with product and engineering teams, and genuine excitement about using AI-enabled tools to transform how work gets done.
* **Vendor Management:** Experience managing vendor partners against clear performance and quality standards.
* **Communication:** Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex problems into actionable updates for leadership and stakeholders.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree required.

**Desired skills and experience**:

* **Healthcare Operations:** Experience in payer operations, utilization management, claims, provider revenue cycle, or a similar high-volume healthcare environment. Prior UM experience is not required.
* **Medicare Advantage Familiarity:** Understanding of Medicare Advantage operations and CMS requirements.
* **Advanced Degree:** MBA or advanced degree in health administration or finance is a plus.
* MBA or advanced degree in health administration or finance is a plus.

Description:

**Job Title:** **Director of Operations**

**Location:** Facility

**Department:** Operations

**Reports To:** VP’s of Operation, COO

**Position Summary**

The Director of Operations is responsible for the overall operational performance and strategic implementation of policies, programs, and systems across substance abuse and mental health treatment facilities. This role ensures service excellence, regulatory compliance, fiscal accountability, and employee engagement while driving operational efficiency and enhancing patient experience. The Director works closely with clinical, administrative, and corporate leadership to support the mission of delivering high-quality, evidence-based behavioral health care.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operational Oversight**

* Direct day-to-day operations across in-patient detox, Residential, and support services.
* Collaborate with Clinical, Nursing, Admissions, HR, and Compliance to ensure alignment of services.
* Develop and implement operational policies and procedures to optimize performance and safety.
* Manage facility licensing and accreditation processes (e.g., Joint Commission, CARF, DCF, SAMHSA).
* Manage overall patient census.

**Strategic Leadership**

* Assist in developing and executing short- and long-term strategic plans.
* Identify opportunities for program enhancements.
* Participate in decision making and contribute to organizational planning.

**Regulatory & Compliance Management**

* Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations related to behavioral health, including HIPAA, OSHA, DOH, Joint Commision, CARF, DEA.
* Lead internal audits and readiness for licensing inspections and third-party reviews.
* Manage Life Safety, Emergency Management, and Environment of Care.

**Team Management & Development**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for all facility staff, while supervising, mentoring, and developing department managers and administrative leadership.
* Support staff development through coaching, training, and performance management.
* Foster a positive work culture that prioritizes ethics, accountability, and inclusivity.
* Apply best practices in recruiting, hiring, and monitoring the onboarding progress of new hires.
* Ensure that all training and corrective actions are conducted consistently, thoroughly documented, and submitted to Human Resources in a timely manner.

**Quality & Performance Improvement**

* Oversee quality assurance initiatives, incident tracking, and risk management.
* Track KPIs related to census, admissions, patient outcomes, and utilization review.
* Use data to implement continuous improvement strategies and drive measurable results.

**Financial & Resource Management**

* Collaborate with Corporate leadership to develop and monitor departmental budgets, forecasts, and cost-containment strategies.
* Ensure responsible utilization of resources and procurement of operational needs.
* Collaborate with Finance to monitor billing, the Utilization Review department, and financial performance.
* Manage Payroll budgets.

**Patient & Community Engagement**

* Promote a patient-centered approach throughout service delivery.
* Referral Management collaboration with business development department.
* Supervise Patient Care Specialists and oversee discharge planning.
* Maintain company hospitality standards and practices.

Requirements:

**Qualifications**

**Required**:

* Minimum 3 years of progressive leadership in a behavioral health, substance abuse, or healthcare setting.
* In-depth understanding of behavioral health regulations and operational requirements.
* Demonstrated success in managing multidisciplinary teams.
* Financial proficiency in budget management.

**Preferred**:

* Experience with Joint Commission, CARF, state and federal regulatory bodies.
* Familiarity with state-specific health department regulations (e.g., DCF in Florida).
* Experience with EMR and CRM software.

**Core Competencies**

* Strategic thinking and execution
* Operational and financial acumen
* Regulatory and compliance expertise
* Crisis management and problem-solving
* Leadership and organizational development
* Communication and relationship building

**Job Description Summary:**

**Location: St. Louis or Kansas City.**

 

This role serves as the steward of our HoReCa & FSOP strategy across our mainstream Bottler Partners. We are looking for candidates with bottling or general management experience who can build relationships and execute our strategies across our network while navigating market dynamics, integrating business strategies, and driving excellence in execution.

 

**What You'll Do for Us**
=========================

 

* Own On‑Premise (Hotels, Restaurants, and Cafés (HoReCa) + Foodservice & On‑Premise (FSOP) + Local Market Plans (LMP for Mainstream bottlers

* Responsible for weekly/monthly performance management, including reporting on revenue, volume, share, and transaction metrics.

* Monitors performance versus execution objectives, re-plans as necessary, and provides feedback to key stakeholders.

* Executes the HoReCa commercial strategy and collaborates directly with bottling partners for local market execution, ensuring the alignment of strategic goals.

* Responsible for collaborating on contingency plans to deliver annual business plan performance, covering key metrics such as revenue, volume, share, net outlets, SOVI (share of visual inventory), and pricing.

* Assess bottler businesses’ high-level strategies and short- vs. long-term decision-making to prevent integration disruptions and ensure feasibility.

* Define and leverage critical measures to evaluate strategic success and align initiatives with the company’s broader goals.

* Collaborate with bottlers to optimize operational bottler-packaging-product-channel (OBPPC) frameworks and local initiatives.

* Navigate channel strategies and develop precise action plans catered to diverse markets to align with profitability and competitive needs.

* Foster strong relationships with local bottlers and external stakeholders by managing governance routines and resolving bottling contracts and national supply chain agreements.

* Negotiate value-driven solutions by leveraging evidence-based arguments and creative, strategic thinking while balancing transactional goals with long-term relationship value.

* Evaluate regional dynamics, consumer demand patterns, and bottler investment needs to optimize strategies.

Ensure real-time reporting and action plans address competitive pressures and enhance market penetration. 

 

**Qualifications & Requirements**
=================================

 

* Bachelor’s degree in business, Finance, Marketing, or Management with a master’s degree preferred.

* 7+ years of experience in a Consumer-Packaged Goods (CPG) or related industry, with a focus on direct sales, key account management, or franchise management. Experience should include proven P&L ownership and the ability to deliver measurable business results.

* Demonstrated success in creating and executing business plans aligned with long-term objectives and informed by deep insights into revenue growth, market conditions, and customer segmentation trends.

* A track record of successfully monitoring performance metrics (revenue, volume, share, transactions) and adapting strategies to achieve positive outcomes. Candidates should be familiar with methodologies for reporting and analyzing key performance indicators (KPIs).

* Expertise in managing a portfolio across diverse distribution channels and customer types. Proven ability to apply market segmentation strategies and action plans that drive region-specific results and improve system efficiency.

* Strong capability to manage, negotiate, and resolve contracts, including National Supply Chain agreements and governance routines, with a focus on maximizing value while maintaining positive relationships. Provides evidence-based, creative solutions during negotiations to achieve win-win outcomes.

Ability to thrive in dynamic environments where priorities shift and market conditions change rapidly. Candidates must have demonstrated experience adapting plans and strategies to navigate uncertainty while maintaining focus on long-term goals.

role.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.
 
 We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.
 
 We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.
 
 If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.
 
 About the Role
 Crusoe is looking for a Director of Accounting to own accounting, cost accounting and financial reporting for its manufacturing business. You'll report to the Corporate Controller and lead a multi-site team of 8+ and act as the accounting partner to Manufacturing leadership. You'll also build the cost, inventory and control infrastructure the business needs as production grows to meet demand for Crusoe's AI infrastructure.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Leadership & Strategy 
 Lead, build and develop a team of 8+ across multiple manufacturing facilities. Set the team's structure, hiring plan and development path as the business grows.

 Act as the primary finance partner to manufacturing leadership (operations, supply chain, engineering, quality and procurement). Turn plant and assembly metrics into financial insight and decisions.

 Drive financial accountability across operations by setting cost targets, tracking performance and influencing decisions on capacity, make-vs-buy, sourcing and pricing.

 Advise executive leadership on product and program margins, cost-reduction opportunities and the financial impact of design, material and process changes.

 Cost Accounting & Inventory 
 Own the cost accounting framework, including standard cost methodology, the annual standard-setting process, overhead absorption and labor rates.

 Set and oversee inventory accounting policy, including valuation, WIP, high-value long-lead components, reserves and excess/obsolete inventory. Own the cycle count and physical inventory programs across all sites.

 Lead analysis of manufacturing variances (purchase price, usage, labor, overhead), yield and productivity. Turn the results into actionable cost-improvement initiatives.

 Own new-product and new-program cost estimates and margin modeling in partnership with Engineering and Sales.

 Close, Reporting & Controls 
 Be accountable for a timely, accurate month-end close for the manufacturing entity. Present results, key drivers and risks to the Controller, CAO and operations leadership.

 Ensure US GAAP compliance and own the manufacturing control environment, building it out to a SOX-ready, audit-ready standard. Serve as the primary contact for external auditors on manufacturing and inventory matters.

 Lead the manufacturing entity's annual budget and rolling forecasts, working with FP&A.

 Systems & Scale 
 Act as the accounting owner for the ERP manufacturing modules (BOMs, routings, work orders, costing) and lead system improvements and implementations.

 Design, document and continuously improve scalable processes, with a focus on automation, as new facilities and product lines come online.

 
 Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in Accounting. CPA or CMA required.

 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 5+ years in manufacturing or cost accounting and 3+ years leading teams (including managers).

 Proven ownership of standard costing, inventory valuation and variance analysis in a complex, multi-site manufacturing environment.

 Deep experience with ERP manufacturing modules (BOMs, routings, job and work-order costing). ERP implementation experience is a plus.

 Experience with complex inventory, such as WIP, engineered-to-order or high-value long-lead components.

 Strong knowledge of US GAAP and internal controls. SOX, public-company or Big 4 experience is a plus.

 Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills.

 High operational credibility: comfortable on the factory floor and able to influence senior operations and engineering leaders.

 Track record of scaling teams, processes and systems in a high-growth environment.

 
 Benefits: 
 Competitive compensation and equity packages

 Restricted Stock Units

 Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 Employer contributions to HSA account

 Paid parental leave

 Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 Mental health & wellness support

 Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 Cell phone stipend

 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 Volunteer time off

 Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 Daily meals allowance

 Additional perks & programs specific to location

 
 Compensation Range 
 Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $185,000 - $215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)

role.title: Director, Commercial Operations
role.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.




ABOUT THIS ROLE



The Director, Commercial Operations will be the operational backbone of Crusoe's Energy Development Group. This person owns the analytical frameworks, pipeline processes, and team capabilities that allow Crusoe to evaluate and advance land and power opportunities at speed and at scale. From complex financial modeling and market analysis to pipeline integrity and board-level reporting, this role ensures the BD team operates with precision and strategic clarity.

This is a leadership-first, analytically grounded role. The ideal candidate brings deep experience in energy project finance or development, a track record of building and mentoring high-performing analyst teams, and the process orientation to continuously raise the quality bar on how Crusoe evaluates and advances opportunities. You will work closely with senior leadership across Energy Development, Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams and will be a key contributor to the operational health of Crusoe's project pipeline.




WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON



 - Overseeing a team of Energy Development Analysts, setting the standard for analytical rigor, process discipline, and professional growth

 - Owning the development and refinement of economic models that underpin power origination and data center site pricing decisions

 - Driving continuous improvement of due diligence workflows, pipeline management processes, and reporting mechanisms across the Energy Development team

 - Overseeing the integrity and accuracy of Crusoe's data center opportunity pipeline, ensuring leadership has a reliable, real-time view of the project portfolio

 - Supervising the creation of board-level presentations, project approval materials, and executive communications that translate analytical complexity into clear strategic recommendations

 - Tracking and synthesizing hyperscaler activity, regulatory developments, and domestic energy infrastructure trends to surface actionable intelligence for the team

 - Supporting cross-functional collaboration between Energy Development and the Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams to move projects efficiently through the development pipeline






CORE RESPONSIBILITIES



Lead and enable the Energy Development Analyst team

 - Support, mentor, and develop a team of analysts, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture

 - Provide hands-on guidance on financial modeling, market analysis, and project evaluation

Drive analytical quality and strategic relevance

 - Oversee the development of detailed economic models for new large-scale land and power opportunities and data center site power pricing

 - Ensure analyses of energy development potential and economics are accurate, rigorous, and decision-ready

 - Guide the team in leveraging internal data analytics tools and external market intelligence to identify and vet opportunities

Own pipeline management and process improvement

 - Drive continuous improvement of business operations processes within the Energy Development team, including project management, due diligence workflows, and reporting mechanisms

 - Maintain the integrity of Crusoe's data center opportunity pipeline, ensuring data accuracy and timely updates

 - Develop and implement best practices for tracking key pipeline metrics and project statuses

Deliver executive-ready reporting and communications

 - Supervise the creation and delivery of board-level presentations, project approval materials, and ad hoc reports for senior management

 - Ensure all communications clearly articulate analytical findings, strategic implications, and support for business decisions

Support cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder engagement

 - Facilitate effective communication between the Energy Development team and the Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams

 - Support the team in communications with external stakeholders including developers, IPPs, and potential partners

Monitor market and regulatory intelligence

 - Oversee tracking and analysis of hyperscaler and co-located data center activity, regulatory changes in the energy sector, and domestic energy infrastructure investments

 - Ensure the team synthesizes this information to identify potential impacts and opportunities for Crusoe




QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - 7+ years of progressive experience in consulting, project finance, investment banking, private equity, energy development, or business operations, with significant focus on the energy sector (renewables, conventional power, or oil & gas)

 - 3+ years of experience in a managerial or team leadership role, with a demonstrated ability to mentor and develop direct reports

 - Deep understanding of energy markets, project economics, and financial modeling

 - Exceptional analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills

 - Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Google Suite; experience with pipeline management systems

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to distill complex analytical and commercial content into clear, executive-ready recommendations

 - Demonstrated ability to build and improve operational processes in a fast-moving, high-ambiguity environment

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field



Preferred

 - MBA or relevant advanced degree

 - Experience with data center infrastructure, HPC, or large-scale power-consuming industries

 - Familiarity with power purchase agreements, offtake structures, and the commercial frameworks that govern energy project development

 - Experience with or strong aptitude for leveraging AI-based tools to drive analytical efficiency and output quality

 - Ability to travel domestically as required (estimated <20%)



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $180,000 -$220,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

role.title: Senior Manager, Protective Operations
role.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

Crusoe is building the infrastructure that powers the AI revolution. As our global footprint expands across data centers, power generation, manufacturing, construction sites, and corporate offices — and as the visibility of our executives and the stakes of our operations continue to rise — the ability to protect our people wherever the business takes them is increasingly critical.

The Senior Manager, Protective Operations will lead Crusoe's executive protection and protective operations programs globally, providing risk-based protection for executives, employees, travelers, and company operations. You will serve as the company's subject matter expert for executive protection, travel risk, protective intelligence, threat management, and sensitive security investigations.

This role will join Crusoe's growing Physical Security organization at a formative moment. You will shape the standards, protocols, vendor network, and operating rhythm that supports Crusoe's expanding global footprint — working closely with the GSOC, the Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst, People, Legal, Communications, Information Security, Facilities, and business leaders to identify risk and translate intelligence into effective protective measures.

The ideal candidate brings experience from U.S. Secret Service, Diplomatic Security Service, high-end executive protection, special operations, or protective details at the national or diplomatic level, and has translated that tradecraft into corporate Protective Operations leadership. You know how to protect people without unnecessarily disrupting the business, and you know how to lead a program that scales.



What You'll Be Working On:

Executive Protection Program Leadership

 - Lead Crusoe's global Executive Protection program, including executive travel, residential considerations, ground transportation, advance work, event coverage, and protective operations

 - Develop risk-based protection strategies based on threat, exposure, location, activity, and other relevant factors rather than title alone

 - Lead security planning for executive appearances, media engagements, conferences, town halls, board activities, major company events, and other high-profile engagements

 - Establish and maintain the standards, protocols, and tradecraft discipline expected of a world-class corporate protection program

Travel Risk Management

 - Own the Travel Risk Management program, establishing processes for pre-travel risk assessment, traveler briefings, high-risk travel, escalation, emergency support, and traveler assistance

 - Conduct advance work and security assessments for domestic and international travel, including hotels, venues, transportation, routes, medical capabilities, and contingency planning

 - Build the duty-of-care framework and escalation procedures that protect Crusoe travelers wherever the business sends them

Protective Intelligence Partnership

 - Partner closely with the Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst and the GSOC to translate protective intelligence into protective action — movement planning, principal protection decisions, advance planning, and threat response

 - Shape the intelligence requirements and collection priorities that support protective operations

 - Operationalize protective intelligence products into daily decisions, travel decisions, and event planning

Threat Assessment and Management

 - Establish and support threat assessment and management processes for workplace violence, threatening communications, stalking, harassment, fixated individuals, concerning behavior, and other potential threats

 - Partner with HR, Employee Relations, Legal, and the Intelligence Analyst on threat cases requiring coordinated response and protective action

 - Apply structured behavioral threat assessment methodologies to differentiate legitimate threats from noise

Sensitive Security Investigations

 - Lead or support sensitive security investigations involving threats, theft, misconduct, unauthorized access, insider risk, security incidents, and suspected fraud in partnership with Legal, People, Internal Audit, Information Security, and other stakeholders

 - Support elevated-risk employee matters, including sensitive terminations, credible threats, domestic violence concerns affecting the workplace, and other situations requiring additional protective measures

 - Maintain investigative discipline, chain of custody, and reporting standards appropriate to the sensitivity of each matter

Site and Geographic Risk Assessment

 - Conduct geographic and site security risk assessments in support of new markets, potential company locations, major projects, and business expansion

 - Evaluate country, city, neighborhood, and site-level risks including crime, political instability, civil unrest, terrorism, emergency response, medical capabilities, transportation, natural hazards, and other relevant threats

 - Produce assessments that inform executive travel, site selection, event planning, and business expansion decisions

Program Development and Vendor Management

 - Develop protective operations plans, standards, protocols, and escalation procedures that scale across a growing global organization

 - Select, manage, and evaluate executive protection, secure transportation, travel security, investigative, and other specialized security vendors globally

 - Grow the vendor network — domestic and international — required to extend Crusoe's protective capabilities wherever the business operates

 - Support budget development, forecasting, and financial management for protective operations programs and vendors

Operational Partnership

 - Coordinate closely with the GSOC during executive travel, elevated-risk events, emerging threats, and critical incidents

 - Establish relationships with law enforcement, government agencies, security partners, and other external organizations relevant to protective operations

 - Support crisis and incident response involving executives, employees, travelers, threats, or other security events

Program Measurement and Maturity

 - Develop metrics and reporting to measure program effectiveness, emerging risks, protective activity, and opportunities for improvement

 - Help mature the Protective Operations function as Crusoe's global footprint and risk profile continue to evolve

 - Maintain discretion and sound judgment when handling highly sensitive executive, employee, investigative, and company information



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 10+ years of experience in executive protection, corporate security, protective intelligence, law enforcement, military protective operations, diplomatic security, or a related field

 - 5+ years leading complex executive protection, protective operations, or corporate security programs

 - Demonstrated experience protecting senior executives and supporting domestic and international travel

 - Strong experience conducting advances, threat assessments, security risk assessments, and protective planning

 - Experience developing and managing executive protection programs in a corporate environment strongly preferred

 - Knowledge of protective intelligence, behavioral threat assessment, workplace violence prevention, and threat management principles

 - Experience conducting or managing sensitive corporate or security investigations

 - Understanding of travel risk management, including international security environments, traveler risk assessment, emergency response, and duty-of-care considerations

 - Experience planning security for media engagements, executive appearances, major events, and other high-profile activities

 - Ability to assess rapidly evolving situations, make sound risk-based decisions, and operate effectively with incomplete information

 - Demonstrated ability to work with senior executives while maintaining discretion, professionalism, adaptability, and confidentiality

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly communicate risk and recommendations to executives and business leaders

 - Experience managing specialized security vendors, executive protection providers, secure transportation providers, and other external partners

 - Ability to collaborate effectively across Legal, People, Communications, Information Security, Facilities, Operations, and other business functions

 - Ability to travel domestically and internationally approximately 30–50%, with periods of increased travel based on operational requirements

 - Ability to respond outside normal business hours when significant protective or security situations require support



Bonus Points

 - Prior service with U.S. Secret Service, Diplomatic Security Service, FBI, DEA, U.S. Marshals Service, or an equivalent federal protective agency

 - Military special operations background with protective detail experience (SOF, MARSOC, Naval Special Warfare, Air Force Special Tactics, or equivalent)

 - Prior corporate executive protection leadership experience within technology, critical infrastructure, data centers, energy, manufacturing, or another rapidly growing global organization

 - Experience leading principal-level protective details for Fortune 500 CEOs, founders, or high-net-worth principals

 - Experience developing enterprise Travel Risk Management or Workplace Violence Prevention programs

 - Experience conducting protective intelligence and open-source threat research

 - Experience supporting international operations and higher-risk travel environments, including gray and amber travel zones

 - Experience working with law enforcement, intelligence, diplomatic, or government security organizations

 - Familiarity with intelligence, case management, mass notification, travel risk, and security operations platforms (Ontic, Dataminr, Everbridge, International SOS, Crisis24, or peer tools)

 - CPP, PSP, PCI, Certified Threat Manager (CTM), ATAP certifications, or other relevant professional credentials

 - Multilingual capability, particularly in languages supporting Crusoe's international footprint



OPERATING CONDITIONS:

 - San Francisco or Denver on-site, with domestic and international travel of approximately 30–50% to support executive protection, advance work, high-risk travel, site assessments, and major events

 - On-call availability for executive travel windows, elevated-risk events, emerging threats, and critical incidents

 - Response outside normal business hours when significant protective or security situations require support

 - Occasional nights, weekends, and holidays as the operational tempo demands

 - Handling of sensitive, confidential, and executive-protection information with appropriate discretion is a core expectation of the role


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

Success in this role means Crusoe has a proactive, intelligence-led, and risk-based protective operations program capable of supporting executives and employees wherever the business operates.

You will lead a program that identifies threats early, provides executives and travelers with appropriate protection without unnecessarily disrupting business, responds effectively to sensitive incidents, and scales as Crusoe expands into new markets and operating environments.

You will also establish a close operating partnership with the GSOC and the Intelligence Analyst: the GSOC maintains global situational awareness and enterprise threat monitoring, the Intelligence Analyst produces protective intelligence assessments, and Protective Operations owns the translation of intelligence into protective action.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 - $260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

role.title: Director / Senior Director, Technical Operations
role.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with  neffy® , the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture. 



 

 THE OPPORTUNITY 

 
 The Director / Senior Director, Technical Operations will provide strategic leadership for ARS' external manufacturing and Technical Operations activities supporting the continued development, lifecycle management, and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical, business, and operational leadership with cross-functional influence and CMO management expertise to drive manufacturing excellence, scalable operations, and reliable product supply.

 This role is accountable for manufacturing strategy, CMO performance, process and technology lifecycle management, resolution of major technical issues, and execution of key Technical Operations initiatives across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Working closely with internal stakeholders and external partners, the position leads complex cross-functional programs, oversees partner performance and agreements, manages departmental planning and budgets, and ensures technical, supply, regulatory, and business risks are appropriately identified, assessed, and escalated.



   ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Provide leadership for Technical Operations programs and external manufacturing activities, establishing strategy, priorities, scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, and key decision points.

 Own senior-level Technical Operations relationships with key CMOs/CDMOs and other external partners; establish governance, performance expectations, escalation pathways, and accountability for delivery against manufacturing and business commitments.

 Provide technical leadership for formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, continued process verification, and manufacturing lifecycle management, as applicable.

 Oversee clinical and commercial manufacturing strategy and execution in coordination with external manufacturers and internal stakeholders; ensure appropriate Technical Operations support for critical manufacturing campaigns, product launches, and supply requirements.

 Provide senior technical review and oversight of manufacturing and process documentation, process performance, significant vendor changes, investigations, annual/product reviews, and significant deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and complex manufacturing problems; ensure robust technical investigation, root-cause analysis, effective corrective and preventive actions, continued process control, and reliable manufacturing in partnership with Quality Assurance.

 Lead technical assessments of significant manufacturing, process, component, and supplier changes and coordinate evaluation of quality, regulatory, supply, financial, and business impacts with appropriate functional stakeholders.

 Establish and review manufacturing, supply, and external partner performance metrics and KPIs, including service, quality, on-time delivery, right-first-time, cost, capacity, and other appropriate measures; drive lifecycle improvements, operational excellence, capacity planning, cost improvement, and risk-reduction initiatives across the external network.

 Lead external partner business and technical governance, including selection and strategic development of CMOs, CDMOs, suppliers, and other critical partners; establish performance expectations and governance mechanisms, oversee business reviews, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, contract and supply agreement support, and escalation of commercial or operational issues; and develop business continuity, capacity, and second-source strategies for critical manufacturing capabilities and materials.

 Represent Technical Operations on cross-functional program and leadership teams; communicate manufacturing strategy, program status, significant risks, financial implications, and recommendations to senior management and key stakeholders.

 Partner with Regulatory Affairs on CMC strategy, regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and health authority responses; ensure manufacturing plans and technical decisions are aligned with regulatory commitments.

 Lead Technical Operations business planning and continuous improvement initiatives, including departmental budget development with Finance/FP&A, contract lifecycle management, operational process standardization, and long-range manufacturing planning.

 Provide leadership and governance for commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including 3PL and distribution partner performance, inventory and supply continuity, shipping/returns interfaces, and support of product launches and new markets.

 Oversee the commercial serialization program, including serialized packaging operations, EPCIS data exchange with trading partners and service providers, and compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements; ensure issues are appropriately escalated and resolved cross-functionally.

 Provide leadership and oversight for clinical supply operations, including clinical material planning, packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and coordination of Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities with Clinical Operations and external vendors.

 
   KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: 

 
 Broad and deep knowledge of cGMP, pharmaceutical manufacturing, quality systems, formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, lifecycle management, and applicable CMC regulatory expectations, with the technical credibility to critically challenge external partner data, conclusions, and recommendations.

 Demonstrated leadership of outsourced manufacturing relationships, complex cross-functional programs, and teams, including governance, performance management, contract/scope management, budgeting, executive-level escalation, influence without direct authority, and accountability of external partners for performance and commitments.

role.title: Director of Risk Management and Quality
role.description:
**JOB SUMMARY:**

**Your experience matters**

At Westpark Springs, we are committed to empowering and supporting a diverse and determined workforce who can drive quality, scalability, and significant impact across our hospitals and communities. In your role, you'll support those that are in our facilities who are interfacing and providing care to our patients and community members. We believe that our collective efforts will shape a healthier future for the communities we serve.

**What we offer**

Fundamental to providing great care is supporting and rewarding our team. In addition to your base compensation, this position also offers:

* Health (Medical, Dental, Vision) and 401K Benefits for full-time employees
* Competitive Paid Time Off
* Employee Assistance Program - mental, physical, and financial wellness assistance
* Tuition Reimbursement/Assistance for qualified applicants
* And much more...

**About Us**

**People are our passion and purpose.** Westpark Springs is a 96 bed hospital located in Richmond, TX and is part of Lifepoint Health, a diversified healthcare delivery network committed to making communities healthier® with acute care, rehabilitation, and behavioral health facilities from coast to coast. From your first day to your next career milestone-your experience matters.

**How you'll contribute:**

Leads and oversees a comprehensive, efficient, and integrated hospital-wide Continuous Quality and Performance Improvement (CQPI) program. Uses data collection, analysis, and trending to assess performance; focuses on process and systems improvement; directs risk management and patient safety activities; investigates adverse outcomes; coordinates regulatory/accreditation readiness; and educates staff on CQPI and related quality programs. **This role is 100% onsite.**

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

**Licensure:** Registered Nurse with current state licensure highly preferred; clinical license required.

**Education:** BSN or BS/BA required.

**Experience:** Minimum two (2) years in an acute hospital or rehabilitation setting required; prior supervisory experience preferred.

**Certifications:** Basic Life Support (BLS/CPR) required; certification preferred by APIC (American Practitioners of Infection Control) and NAHCQ (National Association of Health Care Quality).

**Skills:** Data analysis and reporting; CQPI methodologies (e.g., RCA, FMEA, PDSA); risk management and patient safety facilitation; regulatory/accreditation readiness; effective teaching, communication, and collaboration.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**Job Specific:**

* Provides leadership and oversight of a comprehensive, efficient and integrated organization wide Continuous Quality Performance Improvement program.
* Measures and assesses performance through collection, analyses, and trending of data.
* Focuses on processes and systems to improve performance.
* Directs, facilitates, and reports on all aspects of services relating to risk management and patient safety.
* Investigates factors contributing to adverse outcomes in order to improve processes and systems.
* Encourages reporting on risk reduction strategies in an atmosphere which minimizes blame or retaliation. Fosters environment to reduce unanticipated adverse events and/or outcomes.
* Responsible for education of Continuous Quality and Performance Improvement and additional hospital-wide education and training.
* Directs the functions and operation of the hospital-wide continuous quality improvement program including review of records for indicators of quality; reports findings to leadership, Medical Executive Committee, the Board of Managers and other committees as appropriate.
* Responsible for education of Continuous Quality and Performance Improvement to hospital and medical staff.
* Annually reviews hospital wide plans for the functions of IC and CQPI and establishes goals and objectives for the next year.
* Acts as a liaison to local health officials, coordinates inspections and accreditation reviews with state and other regulatory agencies.
* Demonstrates knowledge of growth, development, and the aging process for the planning and delivery of age-appropriate care.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Skills:**

* Basic computer knowledge.
* Knowledge of basic equipment.
* Appropriate telephone communication skills.

OSHA EXPOSURE DETERMINATION:

* A key element for a successful Exposure Control Plan is to identify situations that place all employees at risk for exposure. To facilitate this, the Hospital maintains a list of job classifications and contact status for all employees in which employees have occupational exposure to bloodborne pathogens. This position has been identified as Category III: Employees who have no occupational exposure to bloodborne pathogens in the normal performance of job duties.

role.title: Director of Operations-Life Sciences
role.description:
**Who we are:**

Charter Medical, part of the Solesis family of companies, specializes in single-use solutions that enable life sciences innovators to turn bold ideas into lasting breakthroughs, supporting industry-leading companies in bringing life-saving therapies to market. Operating in North Carolina, Charter Medical employs more than 150 team members across two facilities in Winston-Salem.

Guided by a commitment to quality, innovation and customer success, Charter partners with customers to transform promising therapies into commercial realities. Employees contribute to solutions that support life-changing treatments and make a meaningful impact on patients around the world.

**1st shift Monday-Friday 8:00 am-5:00 pm**

**About the role:**

The Director of Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the site, with full accountability for Profit & Loss (P&L) performance, manufacturing excellence, and sustainable, profitable growth in single-use cell processing and biopharmaceutical manufacturing. The role translates Charter Medical’s mission into operating priorities that advance purpose-built, customizable processing solutions, reduce the cost and risk of delivering advanced therapies, and enable customers to scale reliably. By aligning capacity, capital investment, innovation, quality, and workforce capability with customer demand, the Director fosters a culture of safety, compliance, responsiveness, collaboration, urgency, and continuous improvement—helping biopharmaceutical innovators make life-changing therapies more accessible to patients.

**What you will do:**

* Lead all site manufacturing operations to ensure safe, compliant, reliable, and profitable execution of customer demand.
* Own site P&L performance, including revenue attainment, EBITDA, gross margin, labor and overhead management, productivity, spending, savings, and budget execution.
* Develop and execute the site operating plan and manufacturing strategy in alignment with company objectives, customer demand, and growth priorities.
* Direct manufacturing execution, facilities, maintenance, and continuous improvement activities to achieve Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and People objectives.
* Ensure effective utilization of labor, equipment, materials, information, and facility capacity to improve throughput, yield, lead time, asset utilization, and on-time delivery.
* Establish, review, and act on key performance indicators and performance trends through daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual operating reviews.
* Evaluate and improve manufacturing methods using knowledge of product requirements, materials, fabrication processes, tooling, equipment capability, work methods, and quality-control standards.
* Lead capacity planning and resource allocation to support current production, new business, customer growth, and future site requirements.
* Develop, justify, prioritize, and execute capital investment plans supporting safety, compliance, capacity, automation, productivity, business continuity, and site growth.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, delivery, yield, scrap, labor productivity, cost reduction, flow, and equipment reliability.
* Ensure product availability through disciplined execution of the production plan and alignment of labor, materials, equipment, and technical support.
* Support new-product introductions, technology transfers, pilot builds, process scale-up, design-for-manufacturability reviews, product validations, and commercialization activities.
* Partner with Commercial and Product Development teams to assess manufacturing capability, support customer opportunities, align operational commitments, and respond to changing demand.
* Serve as the senior manufacturing representative during customer visits, business reviews, audits, regulatory inspections, CAPA activities, and issue-resolution efforts.
* Ensure manufacturing execution meets product specifications, documentation, and traceability requirements and supports compliant delivery.
* Build and maintain robust manufacturing training and qualification programs in partnership with Human Resources.
* Develop annual operating budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, productivity targets, and capital plans; monitor performance and implement corrective actions when results fall below plan.
* Oversee product-costing inputs based on actual manufacturing performance, labor productivity, yields, scrap, material usage, and operational assumptions in partnership with Finance.
* Identify staffing requirements; participate in selection and hiring; build organizational capability to meet operational and growth requirements.
* Coach, mentor, and develop operations leaders and employees; establish clear expectations, provide ongoing feedback, manage performance, and support succession and career development.
* Partner with Human Resources to maintain an effective organization structure, conduct talent reviews, improve employee engagement, and develop leadership capability.
* Foster a culture of safety, accountability, quality, customer focus, collaboration, disciplined execution, and continuous improvement throughout the site.
* Ensure adherence to site safety requirements, PPE practices, environmental expectations, and applicable Health, Safety, and Environmental systems.
* Maintain strong communication across shifts, departments, and leadership so priorities, risks, decisions, and customer commitments are clearly understood.
* Act independently with a high degree of judgment and initiative to resolve complex manufacturing and business issues and develop recommendations for senior leadership.

***Please note that Charter Medical does not provide employment visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship both now or in the future.***

**Who you are:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, life sciences, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including significant experience in a regulated life sciences, biopharmaceutical, medical device, or comparable environment.
* Minimum of 4 years of experience in manufacturing management, plant leadership, or director-level role.
* Demonstrated experience owning or significantly influencing a manufacturing P&L, operating budget, productivity plan, and capital portfolio.
* Demonstrated ability to lead managers and cross-functional teams, coach employees, resolve conflict, and drive accountability.
* Working knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices, FDA expectations, ISO-based quality systems, and regulated manufacturing documentation.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning, equipment capability, facilities, maintenance, cost drivers, and operational workflows.
* Considerable knowledge of ERP systems and proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
* Effective written, verbal, presentation, analytical, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work across shared-service and matrixed organizations.
* Ability to use Lean Six Sigma and structured problem-solving methods to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and business performance.
* Lean Six Sigma certification preferred.
* Experience in cleanroom manufacturing preferred.
* Experience supporting biopharmaceutical customers, customer audits, and contract manufacturing operations preferred.
* Experience leading capacity expansion, automation, technology transfer, or operational transformation initiatives preferred.

**Perks / Benefits:**

* Generous Paid Time Off
* Paid Breaks
* Annual Bonus
* 401(k) with excellent company match
* Health Insurance with multiple plans to choose from
* Paid Short Term and Long Term Disability

Equal Opportunity Employer 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

role.description:
**Title:** **Sr Manager, GCP Quality Assurance**
================================================

Date: Oct 29, 2026

Location: Princeton, NJ

Company: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc (USA)

The Sr Manager, GCP Quality Assurance (Asset Lead) provides strategic quality oversight for assigned development programs within the Sun Pharma Global Development Organization (GDO) Branded Portfolio within Innovative Medicines. The role serves as the primary Quality asset representative to cross-functional global project teams and ensures compliance with applicable GXP regulations, company quality standards, and risk-based quality management principles across the clinical development lifecycle.

 

Key Responsibilities:

* Serve as the primary Quality representative for assigned assets/programs.
* Provide quality risk assessments and strategic recommendations to asset teams.
* Represents QA on the clinical and non-clinical teams; Quality Assurance oversight ensures compliance to regulations, guidance, local laws, and applicable ISO standards, TORO, approved protocol, study plans, risk management, safety and product quality reporting requirements and use of validated systems for patient safety, investigational product quality, and data integrity.
* Plans, conducts, and reports GCP audits of clinical trial sites, CROs, vendors, laboratories, internal processes, computerized systems, and regulatory submission documentation in accordance with applicable regulations and procedures.
* Ensures that the GCP Audit schedules are created and approved by QA management; create and execute audit plans that ensure compliance to applicable regulations, guidance/ guidelines, and standard operating procedures.
* Able to travel to conduct audits onsite at vendors’ facilities, service providers, clinical trial sites, and/or internal Sun systems. Proficient to read/write/review written regulatory submission documents to ensure the content is compliant to regulatory requirements. Performs For-cause/Directed Audits when assigned.
* Supports/ Leads company inspection readiness preparations and hosts inspector onsite and via remote tools; Serves as Sponsor QA to support Clinical Site inspections, as required
* Influence clinical development decisions through quality expertise. Assess quality implications of protocol amendments, study design changes, vendor strategies, and regulatory commitments. Collaborate with Outsourcing, Non-clinical, Clinical teams and functional departments (including clinical supplies and project managers) to support the selection of vendors and service providers based on risk evaluation thru audit; manage complex organizational issues, identify and implement organizational mitigations and/or process improvements.
* Escalate significant quality risks to senior leadership. Monitors quality metrics, audit observations, CAPAs, deviations, and critical quality events to identify emerging trends and risks. Provides regular reporting to senior management and develops proactive mitigation strategies in collaboration with functional stakeholders.
* Support the implementation of procedures and quality systems used to support the GDO Sponsored trials and for audit conduct of vendors, labs, clinical trial sites, and submissions dossiers.
* Travel requirement is 20% domestic and international

Requirements:

* BS Degree in Chemistry, Biology, or related scientific discipline; advanced degree preferred. A minimum of 10 years of experience in clinical research, clinical quality assurance, or GxP-regulated environments within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, or clinical research organizations.
* Demonstrated expertise in ICH-GCP, FDA, EMA, ISO and global regulatory requirements.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and inspection readiness programs.
* Experience providing quality oversight to Phase I-IV clinical development programs.
* Strong risk-based quality management and stakeholder influencing skills; ability to communicate with technical and non-technical colleagues; experience establishing and maintaining effective relationships with leaders and peers.

* Demonstrated capability as organizational change agent. Ability to lead and participate on teams with shared responsibility for outcomes and decision-making.

The presently-anticipated base compensation pay range for this position is $150,500 to $183,500. Actual base compensation may vary based on a number of factors, including but not limited to geographical location and experience. In addition, this position is part of the Annual Performance Bonus Plan. Employees are eligible to participate in Company employee benefit programs which include medical, dental and vision coverage; life insurance; disability insurance; 401(k) savings plan; flexible spending accounts; and the employee assistance program. Employees also receive various paid time off benefits, including vacation time and sick time.

 

The compensation and benefits described above are subject to the terms and conditions of any governing plans, policies, practices, agreements, or other materials or documents as in effect from time to time, including but not limited to terms and conditions regarding eligibility. If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company, or individual department/team performance, and market factors.

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Why We Stand Out**

Seeking a career-defining opportunity where your leadership, strategic vision, and client expertise are recognized and rewarded? Kaufman Rossin might be just the place for you.

As one of the top accounting firms in the country, our foundation is “people first.” In the words of James Kaufman, “we prioritize our people, their development, and their well-being. Our values are translated into action every day.”

Kaufman Rossin is a privately owned, independent public accounting firm, which means we are not beholden to outside investors or private equity influence. This independence allows us to prioritize long-term client relationships, maintain objectivity in our advisory approach, and make strategic decisions that benefit our people and clients, not external stakeholders. Our structure fosters agility, entrepreneurial thinking, and a collaborative culture where leadership is accessible, and innovation is encouraged.

Celebrated as the Best Place to Work in South Florida over a dozen times, Kaufman Rossin has grown to over 700 employees, with offices spanning the tri-county area, including sister entities Kaufman Rossin Wealth and Kaufman Rossin Alternative Investment Services.

**Think you have what it takes?**

**How You'll Contribute**

Kaufman Rossin is seeking a **Director of Operations** to lead firm-wide initiatives, strengthen operational practices, and turn strategy into execution. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and partnering closely with the Chief Information Officer and firm leadership, you’ll lead our project managers and business analysts while driving technology implementations, process improvements, and organizational change.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys understanding how the business works, staying close to the details, and improving the experience of our clients and colleagues.

* Lead and develop project managers and business analysts, setting priorities, removing roadblocks, and ensuring consistent, high-quality delivery.
* Oversee multiple firm-wide initiatives, balancing scope, timelines, resources, and business impact while staying actively involved in requirements, planning, testing, and rollout.
* Lead the operational side of technology implementations, from selection and requirements through deployment, adoption, and ongoing optimization, in partnership with the CIO and IT team.
* Drive change management through communication, training, and adoption planning, recognizing how people and culture influence success.
* Develop and maintain policies, procedures, and best practices, and implement process improvements across departments.
* Establish business plans, key performance indicators, and performance targets; monitor results through reporting, audits, and scorecards.
* Ensure compliance with professional standards, regulatory requirements, and internal quality programs while identifying and addressing operational risks.
* Oversee team hiring, staffing, training, performance discussions, and career development, fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Manage budgets, forecasts, and the financial performance of operational initiatives, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and profitability.
* Partner with the COO and firm leadership on strategic and growth initiatives that enhance the client and colleague experience.

 
**Requirements**

**How You'll Contribute**

* 7+ years of related operations, project, or program management experience.

* 10+ years of supervisory leadership experience, ideally managing project managers, business analysts, or similar teams.
* Demonstrated success leading technology implementations and organizational change, with a strong understanding of the process from requirements through adoption.
* A hands-on leadership style, strong emotional intelligence, and the ability to manage multiple initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
* Strong analytical, organizational, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, supported by sound judgment.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with partners, executives, and staff.
* Proficiency with project management and operational reporting tools.
* Availability for occasional travel to support leadership alignment, training, and firm-wide initiatives.

**How You'll Stand Out**

* Experience in professional services, particularly accounting, finance, risk management, or consulting.
* Bachelor’s degree.
* PMP, Prosci, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certifications.
* Experience with Microsoft Office, Salesforce, Domo, Power BI, or generative AI tools.

 
**Benefits**

***We embrace authenticity.*** *Kaufman Rossin is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a culture that reflects the diversity of our firm and clients. We encourage understanding, acceptance, and celebration among all people. That includes lifestyle, education, experience, race, ethnicity, age, religion,* *physical ability, sexual orientation, and gender identity.* ***Differences make unique varieties.***
